articleTitle: The atlas power-flow system - A status report
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The design requirements, design features, test results and status of the Atlas high-energy pulsed-power facility power flow system are described

articleTitle: Neutron production in super-fast deuterated Z-pinches
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In the experiments with profiled agar-agar cylindrical loads filled with deuterated polyethylene, at Z-pinch currents up to 2.7 MA, the neutron radiation of several nanoseconds duration and energies of neutrons of 2.5 MeV, corresponding to D-D reaction neutrons, was registered. The time integrated neutron yield was 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> neutrons per one shot. The neutron radiation appeared at the time when hard X-ray radiation with quanta energies h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">υ</inf> > 30 keV was generated at the stage when the hot (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf> = 3–13 keV) dense (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>) plasma in the Z-pinch neck was forming. The carried out neutron radiation measurements, when only single Z-pinch neck is developed show the correlation of neutron production time with a short time of high temperature plasma existence in this neck.

articleTitle: Fundamental studies of a helical magnetic flux compression generator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The design of a helical flux compression generator, driven by 200 g of high explosives, for basic studies is presented and experimental results are discussed. Generator current and dI/dt are measured with Rogowski coils placed on the load. Both crowbar closure and contact velocity have been successfully simulated with CTH, a three-dimensional finite element hydrodynamic code. The generator's magnetic field structure is briefly discussed and magnetic field probe measurements are presented.

articleTitle: Tunable L-band and S-band gigawatt vircators with feedback
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A concept of feedback vircator with e-beam premodulation was developed and tested. In experiment, ∼1 GW, 20 – 30 ns microwave pulses were produced in L- and S-bands at 5 – 6 % efficiency. The microwave generation was narrow-band with the frequency stable during the pulse. Frequency control within 10 – 20 % was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Lengthening of microwave pulse in a 3-GW relativistic BWO
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Low-energy, high-current electron beam treatment of slow-wave structure was proposed to prevent spontaneous microwave pulse shortening in an X-band relativistic BWO at gigawatt level of output power. As a results, 3-GW, ∼30 ns microwave pulses were produced while the increase in the microwave pulse length and energy was a factor of four.

articleTitle: All solid-state switched pulser for the application of automotive exhaust gas purification
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper describes an all solid-state switched pulser for the application of automotive exhaust gas purification. By using the 24V battery as input energy source, the proposed pulser could produce 10kV, 200A, 100ns pulses at repetition rates up to 20kHz and it is composed of a high efficient DC-DC converter and several pulse generating modules which are connected in series to obtain higher pulse voltage. Each pulse generating module contains MOSFETs, energy storage capacitor and pulse transformer. In this paper, we compared two kinds of circuit topology for DC-DC converter of the pulser and suggested over-voltage and over-current protections of pulser for the reliable operation. Experimental results show that the proposed pulser is very efficient in air pollution control application.

articleTitle: High-power electron beam generator MIG
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A versatile X-ray source has been designed based on a unitary pulse power system. The source makes it possible to perform investigation and tests in a wide range of quantum energy. A line pulse transformer with a stored energy of 250 kJ is used as a base for powering the system [1]. The design of a multi-purpose pulse generator (MIG) is a quite reasonable step in applying and developing the ideas and principles tried out in the systems SGM and SNOP [1–5]. The main idea of the work was to design a rather cheap versatile system allowing generation of high-power X-ray pulses in a varying range of quantum energy and studies on generation of high-power electron and ion beams as well. An analysis has shown a capacitive energy store with an energy < 300 J to be suitable. To form pulses of varying duration and voltages, use was made of wire opening switches, plasma opening switches, and fast forming lines.

articleTitle: 1-MV, 500-Hz all-solid-state nanosecond driver for streamer corona discharge technologies
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: For commercial applications of pulsed power an all-solid-state nano-second driver has been developed. The driver is based on SOS-technology and designed to deliver 40 to 60-ns pulses with an amplitude of up to 1 MV at a 500-Hz repetition rate into electron beam or streamer corona discharge load. An output average power is up to 30 kW. A distinctive feature of the driver is that it uses all solid state switching system. As a final power amplifier an inductive store and a semiconductor opening switch (SOS) are used. The SOS is pumped by a magnetic pulse compressor. Thyristor charging unit is used at the input of the driver. The driver is 3.5 meters long and weighs about 2.5 tons. The design of the driver and experimental results are presented. The results of the first experiments on ignition of large volume streamer corona discharges in atmospheric air are also presented.

articleTitle: Getting short bunches from a 2-MeV electron injector
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A 2-MeV electron injector for the Novosibirsk high-power FEL driven by a 100-MeV racetrack microtron-recuperator was built and commissioned in 1998. It is intended to supply electron bunches of ∼100 ps duration and repetition rate up to 22.5 MHz with average and peak current 45 mA and ∼20 A respectively. The RF-system of the injector is designed to provide stable operation under heavy beam loading. Various problems of bunching and beam transport in the injector are discussed. A number of experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Relativistic plasma microwave sources based on slow plasma mode
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper is devoted to the experimental study of a plasma microwave oscillator and plasma microwave amplifier. The tunable frequency oscillator (from 7 to 28 GHz) gives power ∼50 MW. Emission spectrum is wide ∼30%. Mean frequency dependence on plasma density coincides with theory. In order to narrow the Cherenkov plasma maser emission spectrum plasma microwave amplifier was investigated. The amplified power level 4÷8 MW was achieved in two frequencies 9.1 and 12.9 GHz. The bandwidth was less than 5% in this case.

articleTitle: Processes of material surface modification under combined treatment by pulsed ion beams of different power and plasma flows
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The investigations results are presented for some processes occurring at different stages of strong adhesion coatings and modified layers creation with the use of high-dose implantation and deep diffusive doping of elements under pulsed energetic impact. The investigations have been carried out on the installation providing the possibility of combined materials treatment with pulsed ion beams of power density ranged from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The facility includes the accelerator of high-power ion beams and the sources of repetitively-pulsed metal ion beams and metal plasma flows.

articleTitle: Generation of double pulses with extreamly short pulse reptetition interval by a single pulse forming line system
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new type of double pulse generator is developed to generate independent two pulses with short interval. The system consists of a step-up transformer circuit and a discharge switch free Blumlein pulse forming line, both of which utilizes amorphous metallic cores. At pulse interval T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> ≥ 500 µs (equivalent rep-rate 2 kHz), the system was successfully operated with good reproducibility and produces two pulses of 400 kV with efficiency of 65 %. To enhance the recovery of hydrogen switch, a magnetic switch is used, which enables the operation at T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> ≥ 39 µs (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 26 kHz).

articleTitle: Shock wave production in plane lead targets under action of soft X-ray flux generated by Z-pinch plasma implosion and influence of attendant magnetic field and e-beams
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental production of shock waves with pressure magnitude in shock wave front up to 3 Mbar in plane lead targets under action of soft X-ray flux with power density up to 4*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is under investigation. Soft X-ray source was produced by fast Z-pinch implosion of plasma of the hollow cylindrical loads. Brightness temperature of produced soft X-ray source was varied in range 50 – 85 eV. The soft X-ray pulse duration was changed in range 6 – 20 ns. Shock waves were excited in plane sample layers with thickness 200–400 µm. Spectral brightness of light emission from rear surface side of plane substance layer irradiated by soft X-ray flux from front surface side was recorded by the two-channel visible range pyrometer to measure color temperature during shock wave exit at rear side of substance free surface. Possible initial density changes during experiment as result of preheat due to influence of electron beam, strong magnetic field, and the precursor prepinch generation which are attendant to fast current implosion process were taken into account.

articleTitle: Measurement of the angular spectrum of electrons in a high-current magnetized REB with microsecond duration
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Distribution of electron trajectories over pitch-angles in strong magnetic field are studied. High current density and pulse duration ∼ 1 µs do not hinder to distinguish small pitch-angles (∼ 1°) by the new method. The explosive cathode of proposed construction generates high-current annular REB with absolutely stable shape and pitch-angles not exceeding 4° throughout microsecond pulse.

articleTitle: Improved bremsstrahlung targets for multiterawat modular x-ray generators
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This presentation describes the results of electron beam injection, propagation and conversion to bremsstrahlung radiation at Naval Research Laboratory's Gamble II and on Kharkiv National University Nadia facilities. The objective of the experiments is to evaluate this technique for potential application as an energy density compression technique on the Decade-Quad multi-modular radiation simulator. Initial experiments performed on these generators were reported at the 12<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> International Pulsed Power Conference [1].

articleTitle: Improvement of the corrosion resistance of steels and MCrAlY coatings by application of a pulsed electron beam
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The pulsed electron beam facility GESA I which provides a beam of up to 10 cm diameter, was used to improve the oxidation and corrosion resistance of martensitic steels and of high temperature protective MCrAlY coatings by melt restructuring of the surface. It is shown that corrosion of OPTIFER IVc steel by liquid lead containing 8·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> at% oxygen is avoided by alloying of Al into the surface. The tests so far run 3000 h at 550 °C under control of the oxygen concentration by the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O ratio in an Ar gas atmosphere above the lead. Treatment of the MCrAlY coating on turbine blade specimens leads to higher oxidation resistance at 950 °C and to excellent adherence of Yttria-stabilized zirconia thermal barrier coatings even after 5000 h of exposure to air.

articleTitle: Suppression of ion emission and pinching using heated tantalum anodes in high-power electron-beam diodes
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Pulse-heating tantalum anodes to > 2200 K results in drastic changes to ion emission and beam dynamics. The ion current starts later, the peak ion current is reduced, and beam pinching is suppressed or eliminated. The diode current follows a single-species Child-Langmuir formula until the voltage exceeds 1 MV, then follows a critical current formula, indicating that ions have little effect on the diode impedance. The experiments indicate a definite dependence on different heating procedures. This technique can be used to improved x-ray production on high-power generators such as Decade.

articleTitle: Gas puff implosion measurements and modeling
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Two-dimensional interferometric images obtained in gas-puff z-pinch experiments on the Hawk generator are compared with snowplow calculations using the measured gas distribution for various times during the 250-ns implosion. To match the calculated implosion time with the observed implosion time, 88% to 101% of the measured cathode current, adjusted for each shot, is required to implode the snowplow. The snowplow model reproduces the (r,z) shape of the measured 2-D plasma shell at different times during the implosion. The inferred current loss between the measurement location (17-cm upstream of the nozzle) and the z-pinch may be due to vacuum flow resulting from the plasma-opening switch.

articleTitle: Diagnostics of electron beam for Novosibirsk high-power FEL
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The diagnostics of 2-MeV electron injector for the Novosibirsk high average power FEL based on microtron-recuperator are described. The beam diagnostic system includes beam position monitors, peak and average beam current monitors, and optical diagnostics with the use of optical transition radiation screen. The parameters of this devices and the results of the measurements are presented. The scheme and possibilities of the future optical diagnostic station for microtron-recuperator are proposed and discussed.

articleTitle: Boundary layer formation in a flow of collisionless magnetized plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In the devices, such as plasma accelerators, plasma opening switches, plasma focus, plasma with magnetic field frozen in it moves along electrodes in the direction transversal relative to magnetic field. Near the plasma-surface interface a boundary layer arises where ions colliding with the wall are partly absorbed in an electrode matter and partly go out back to the flow with a loss of momentum and energy. A self-consistent collisionless interaction of the reflected ions with the basic flow ions results in ion gyration of the basic flow towards the electrode. An instability arises, because of which more and more ions collide with the wall leading to anomalous “viscosity” on a scale of ion Larmor radius. The paper solves one-dimensional problem of the near-electrode layer in low density plasma using the particle-in-cell method and assuming that all values depend only on the coordinate perpendicular to the electrode surface. It is shown that the ion scattering on electrode leads to plasma flow deceleration at a distance of ∼0.5 Larmor radius calculated by plasma flow velocity in a wide range of plasma flow Alfven-Mach numbers.

articleTitle: Electron energy measurement for induction linear accelerator “ETIGO-III”
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Induction Linear accelerator “ETIGO-III” (8 MV, 5 kA, 30 ns) is a intense, pulsed, relativistic-electron-beam (IREB) generator designed for applications in material science, high-power microwave generation, pulsed X-ray emission and environmental studies. It consists of four acceleration units, each of them applies a pulsed voltage of 2 MV on the IREB. The IREB is guided by a magnetic field through the four units so that the electron kinetic energy reaches 8 MeV. The time-resolved, spatial distribution of the IREB has been measured by using a Faraday cup with mask electrode. The maximum IREB current density of ∼ 140 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is obtained. The kinetic energy of IREB has been also measured by a magnetically deflection method. The kinetic energy of IREB is estimated to be up to ∼ 7 MeV.

articleTitle: The experimental study of four kinds of helical explosive-driven magnetic field compression generators
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Four kinds of helical explosively driven magnetic field compression generators (MFC) have been developed in our laboratory in recent years. In this paper, some experiment results about these generators are reported and some preliminary conclusions are also offered.

Author Keywords: explosively driven magnetic field compression generators

articleTitle: Generation of 1013 R/S dose power gamma radiation on 240 KJ MIG facility with POS
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper presents experimental results on the shot pulse (< 20 ns) γ-ray generation. The experiments were carried out on the MIG facility, which consists of 240 kJ high voltage linear pulse transformer (LPT), two water lines, vacuum inductive energy storage (IES), plasma opening switch (POS) and diode. The POS parameters have been experimentaly optimized to achieve the maximum POS impedance and coupling with the parameters of initial storage and the electron diode load. The record γ-ray radiation parameters for this type of accelerators, and nearly absolutely ones, were obtained: dose power (1÷2)·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> R/s on 2÷3 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> R/s on 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at the downstream face of the bremsstrahlung target.

articleTitle: Preparation of ultrafine powders using target ablation by high-power ion beam of nanosecond duration
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of morphological and phase analyses of ultrafine powder obtained by ablation of aluminium and steel targets by a pulsed high-power ion beam are presented in the paper. The beam parameters: ion energy of 350 keV, current density of 250–300 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, pulse duration of 60 ns. The dimensions of obtained particles are in the range from 2.5 up to 700 nm. The data of angular separation of particles from a target are presented. An angle in which the main fraction of particles propagates is 30–40°.

articleTitle: Development of high power, high voltage dc power supply for pulsed-power applications and accelerators
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A high-Power and high-voltage dc power supply has been developed for the accelerators and pulsed power applications based on series resonant converter technology. The dc power supply adopted a 31.2 kHz IGBT series resonant snubber-less inverter. The performance test was carried out for two applications, for dc power supply and for capacitor charging power supply. As the dc power supply, output power of 48 kW and 67 kW were obtained under the continuous operation and interval that of 50% duty, respectively. As the capacitor charging power supply, the output energy E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">chg</inf> of 12.0 J and peak charge rate P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">chg</inf> of 46.0 kJ/s were obtained.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic study of the magnetic field, ion dynamics and electron density evolution in a plasma opening switch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Spatially resolved measurements in a planar microsecond POS, using spectroscopy of dopants in the plasma together with charge-exchange spectroscopy, are presented. Measurements of the axial ion velocities together with the B-field and the plasma density evolution show pushing of the protons ahead of the magnetic field together with field penetration into the carbon plasma. A plasma density drop, which leads to the switch opening, was observed during the field penetration into the carbon plasma. The pushing of protons causes plasma flow into the vacuum region between the POS and the load and influences the energy coupling to the load. These results demonstrate the great importance of the effects associated with a multicomponet plasma and makes the plasma composition an important parameters influencing the POS operation. Measurements with a reversed polarity of the POS do not show any significant difference in the magnetic field and the electron density evolution, as predicted by the electron magnetohydrodynamic theory, implying the field penetration is not dominated by Hall penetration. Alternatively, the observed penetration could also be associated with an anomalous collisionality, which would also explain the observed broad current channel. However, so far, no mechanism predicting such a high collisionality has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Characteristics of flat-top nanosecond-pulse breakdown of gas-insulated gaps
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Breakdown characteristics of the statistical time lag and the formative time lag of flashover have been investigated by applying a flat-top nanosecond pulse to dry-air insulated gaps at atmospheric pressure. As for the formative time lag of the sphere gap, the formative time lag was inversely proportional to the electric field. The statistical time lag depended on the gap length for almost the cases.

articleTitle: Definition of parameters of a current shell by electrotechnical measurements in liner implosion experiments on installation Angara-5-1
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The voltage between the anode and cathode of liner unit on Angara-5-1 feels the liner implosion. Temporal dependence of inductance of the liner unit, the flux of electromagnetic power and energy, power and work to increase liner energy were determined by means of measured current and voltage.

articleTitle: Experimental study of a large diameter backward wave oscillator without guiding magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A large diameter backward wave oscillator (BWO) without guiding magnetic field is demonstrated experimentally. The beam propagation is achieved by filling slow wave structure (SWS) with helium or nitrogen gas. The microwave power peaks at nearly 120 mtorr for helium gas and at nearly 8 mtorr for nitrogen gas. Two distinct radiation modes from the BWO are observed and are controlled by the applied beam voltage. One is dominated by axisymmetric TM modes and the other is dominated by non-axisymmetric TE modes. The maximum output power is of the order of 1 kW, which corresponds to electronic efficiency less than 0.1 %. A self-consistent field theory naturally predicts oscillations of non-axisymmetric TE as well as axisymmetric TM. Radiation modes from the BWO without magnetic field can be explained by interactions between normal electromagnetic modes of SWS and degenerate slow space charge beam mode at zero-magnetic field.

articleTitle: Cluster ion control by simultaneous irradiations of high intensity femtosecond laser and nanosecond laser pulse
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Recently, much attention has been focused upon generation of ionized particles from solid target by coulomb explosion using high intensity and ultrashort pulse laser since the high intensity electric field can easily ionize to the maximum charge of the element. This paper reports the generation of molecular carbon ions and decrease of multiple charged ions in case of irradiation of low power nanosecond laser pulse prior to femtosecond laser pulse. The changes in the ion current waveform have been analysed by time of flight measurement with 76.4cm of drift section. This observed waveform was interpreted using energy conservation law.

articleTitle: Multi-wire array implosion physics study and “MOL” test-bed for “Baikal” project based on 900 MJ inductive storage
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Double liner implosion approach for x-ray production and distinction between gas-puff and wire array implosions are described. The test-bed for multi MJ x-ray generator «Baikal» named as “MOL” is presented.

articleTitle: Ion beam modification of carbon fibre
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Surface treatment of high modules carbon fibres by pulse ion (C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) beams have been carried out and changes in morphology and structure of carbon fibres have been investigated by using scanning electron microscopy and electrical resistance measurement.

articleTitle: Optimization of generator using electron beam and electric gas spark discharge for hard-rock destruction
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The report studies the destruction and splitting of hard-rocks by pulsed e-beam and by electric gas spark discharge. It demonstrates that intense repetitive electron beam of sub-microsecond duration destructs the surface effectively for a variety of rocks. An optimum beam density has been obtained for several beam energies to achieve the minimum specific destruction energy capacity. In electric breakdown of hard-rocks material surface insulation and special electrode geometry were used in the blast region to avoid a surface breakdown between electrodes and to produce volume breakdown. The results obtained lead to acquiring of non-expensive technique of excavation of rocks in mining and in destruction and utilization of unusable concrete blocks.

articleTitle: Production of compact long-lived plasma formation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: New method of plasmoid formation is described in the given paper. Conditions of its formation are determined. The first experiments, where it was possible to from the plasmoid, are described.

articleTitle: High-voltage pulse capacitor
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The design and results of the new high-voltage pulse capacitor with diameter of 102 mm, length of 1200 mm, operation voltage 35 kV and power intensity 1 kJ intended for operation as a component of the hole electrohydraulic installations are presented in the report.

articleTitle: Plasma wake-field acceleration of charged particles by selfmodulated long relativistic electron bunch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High-amplitude plasma wake-waves are excited by high-density relativistic electron bunches (REB) moving in a plasma. The wake- fields can be used to accelerate charged particles, to serve as electrostatic wigglers in free-electron plasma lasers (FEL), and also can find many other applications.

articleTitle: Formation of boron heavily doped nanolayer in silicon by recoil implantation using high-intensive power ion beams
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This work was dedicated to the research of possibility to form a nano-sized highly doped boron near-surface layers in silicon. Forming such layers will make it possible to vary the potential barrier height on metal-semiconductor interface. Implantation of boron atoms into the silicon substrate was conducted by the recoil implantation method irradiating the boron film deposited onto the silicon surface by Al-ion high power beams (current density 4–10 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, ion energy 30–150 keV/Z). Analysis of thus made structures by SIMS and measurement of structure's electrical parameters certificates that the near-surface 10 nm thick conductive layer with the charge carrier concentration greater than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup> is created.

articleTitle: Unstable behavior of an exploding wire array for z-pinch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper, the unstable behavior of a wire array is discussed. The instability occurs by the deviation from the homogeneous current flow through many wires. The expressions discriminating between the stability and the instability are derived. Using the resistivity variation of the wire, the unstable behavior during the explosion of the wires is predicted and the tendency to an unstable behavior is evaluated. Also, the unstable behavior of the wire array was confirmed in the wire explosion experiment generally used to produce the z-pinch. The current measurement of parallel exploding wires shows inhomogeneous current flow through the wires. Time-resolved pictures show asymmetrical explosions of the wires.

articleTitle: Mirror-trapped plasma heated by high-power millimeter wave radiation as an ECR source of soft X-rays
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Line soft X-ray emission of pulse electron-cyclotron resonance (ECR) discharge in Argon sustained by powerful beam of millimeter waves in a mirror magnetic trap was investigated. X-ray spectrum in a range 6–17 nm has been obtained, absolute spectral intensity of radiation in this range has been determined. It was shown that such discharge is an effective source of soft X-ray radiation with conversion efficiency of microwaves into X-rays on a level of 10% and with spectral power maximum of 7.3 kW/nm at wavelength of 9 nm.

articleTitle: Characteristics of (Cr1−x, Alx) N films prepared by pulsed laser deposition
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Chromium aluminum nitride ((Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) N) films have been successfully prepared by pulsed laser deposition (PLD). The (Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) N film, which is hard and resistant against wear and oxidation, is one of the most promising pseudobinary nitrides for applications in the protective coatings. The film was synthesized by depositing chromium and aluminum metal vapors in nitrogen. Experiments were carried out by changing the surface area ratio of the target (Al/(Cr+Al)) from 0 to 100%. The hardness of the (Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1−x</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) N films showed the maximum value (HV∼3000) at x = 0.75. Phase transition from B1 (NaCl) structure to B4 (würtzite) structure occurred above x = 0.75, being in a reasonable agreement with the theoretical prediction. As a result of oxidation test, the CrN film oxidized at near 600°C, whereas the (Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>, Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</inf>) N film was not detected the existence of oxide in the annealing temperature range R.T. to 900°C.

articleTitle: Compact SOS-based 400-keV electron beam accelerator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A compact high-current nanosecond accelerator has been designed and tested for experiments concerned with removal of toxic organic impurities from air. This accelerator provides the electron energy up to 400 keV, the beam current of 0.25 to 1.1 kA, the pulse length from 30 to 40 ns, the pulse repetition rate of 200 Hz continuously and up to 1 kHz in 30-second burst mode. The accelerator is based on a SM-3N nanosecond generator that has an all-solid-state switching system with an inductive storage and a semiconductor opening switch (SOS). The vacuum chamber houses an extended metal-ceramic explosion- emission cathode 5-mm wide and 750-mm long. The outlet window is 80 mm wide and 850 mm long.

articleTitle: Implosion of the liner to the thick al wire
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper an implosion of the wolfram wire array to the Al wire target located in the liner center axis is presented. The discharge was operated with a maximal current of 2 – 3 MA and a rise time of ∼100 ns. The Al wire of 250 µm diameter stabilized the phase of the minimum radius. The evolution of the plasma was studied by various x-ray time resolved diagnostics and the Al K-shell lines were registered.

articleTitle: Preperation and characterization of carbon nitride thin film by ionbeam evaporation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The preparation of a C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> thin film has been tried by the ion-beam evaporation method. Clear X-ray diffraction line was not observed. The hydrogen composition decreases and the nitrogen composition increases when the substrate temperature rises. The hardness of the thin film was found to be 1GPa.

articleTitle: Electron linac for industrial applications
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The accelerator has become widely used for industrial field. In particular, the low energy electron accelerator has attracted considerable attention in the field. We have developed and manufactured the electron linac up to 10MeV such as the electron beam sterilization system and the lattice defects generator. The design of electron linac and some of their applications are described in this paper.

articleTitle: Experimental study of the pseudospark switches
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The self-breakdown characteristics (SBC) of pseudospark switches (PSS) with different structure have been experimentally investigated. Two kinds of double-stage PSS with unique structure have been developed. One possesses intermediate cavity electrode and there are two co-axial holes on upper and lower wall. The another one possesses a plane intermediate electrode with three off axially arranged holes. The SBC of the two kinds of two-gap PSS are shifted to higher-pressure range compared with the single-gap PSS and the ordinary two-gap PSS. They are suitable for developing high hold-off voltage PSS.

articleTitle: X-ray spectra of argon and iron ions in a gas-puff z-pinch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: X-ray spectra of Ar gas-puff z-pinch plasma has been measured with a focusing spectrograph with Johansson type quartz crystal. The obtained spectra showed the presence of K-alpha lines of low ionized ions of Fe and Ar. Intensive electron beam with energy not less than 7 keV was detected by x-ray line measurements.

articleTitle: High enegy density plasma produced by pulsed high current discharge of powder
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A plasma created from copper powder was successfully obtained in pulsed high current discharges. Powder flow was injected transiently between the electrodes in vacuum. The powder particles are spherically shaped and are accelerated by pulsed electrostatic field. Diverging powder flow was controlled to form a directed flow with a constant diameter by applying an extra focusing electrode. The powder particle trajectory is numerically analyzed to design the focusing electrode. Conical shaped light emission from the particles was observed in framing photographs during the early stage of discharge.

articleTitle: Characteristics of ion beams produced in a plasma focus device
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Characteristics of the ion beams produced in a plasma focus device were studied. In the experiment, a Mather type plasma focus device was used and it was pre-filled with 2.3 Torr H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The plasma focus device capacitor bank of 43.2 µF was charged to 30 kV to get a peak current of 350 kA. Ion spices and their energy spectrums were evaluated using a Thomson parabola spectrometer, and the particle pinhole image was obtained with an aluminum filtered particle pinhole camera. While, the ion current density was measured with a biased ion corrector. The proton beam energy was distributed from 0.15 MeV to 2 MeV. On the other hand, we found singly and multiply ionized ions of C, N,. The particle pinhole image of the proton beam, which has energy more than 1MeV, was spot type. The ion current density of 1200A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was obtained. The peak power brightness for the proton beams was 18 GW / cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> / Sr /keV.

articleTitle: New frontiers ahead of the fusion of cryogenic and pulsed-power sciences
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Two major research topics were investigated to find out new and useful results under the combination of pulsed power and cryogenic technology. The first major topic was the measurement of pulsed ion beams, which was divided into two minor topics concerning the divergence angle of medium mass ion beam on the cryogenic anode, and the use of CCD element to measure the beam specie and energy. The second major topic was cryogenic target ablation with pulsed ion beams, which was divided into two minor topics concerning the diagnostics of ablated plumes, and the thin film formation and the diagnostics. For respective items, the experimental methods, the preliminary results, and the plans for the near future are shown briefly.

articleTitle: Progress in rod pinch electron beam diodes as intense x-ray radiography sources
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Rod-pinch electron beam diodes were reintroduced at BEAMS'98 as small-diameter intense x-ray sources after a twenty-year hiatus. Much progress has been made recently in both analytical and particle-in-cell numerical modeling of the diode behavior and in obtaining intense x-ray sources for pulsed radiography. Rod-pinch diodes utilize a thin annular cathode surrounding a small-diameter anode rod extending through and beyond the plane of the cathode. Extensive experimental data have been obtained on the NRL Gamble facility between 1 and 2 MV at 20 to 80 kA with 50 ns FWHM. Circuit analysis has been used to study electrode-plasma evolution which dominates the time-dependent diode-impedance behavior, and PIC simulations have been used to study electron and ion dynamics. These are providing a complete picture of diode operation from initial space-charge-limited flow, to magnetically-limited flow, to ion-induced electron beam propagation and, finally, to a tightly focused pinch on the rod tip. Use of the rod pinch for x-ray radiography provides substantial improvement over previously available sources. Typically, < 1-mm-diam spot sizes are measured in the forward direction with doses in the 1 to 3 Roentgen range, 1 meter from the source.

articleTitle: Energy transfer from high-power E-beam to dense plasma at the GOL-3-II facility
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of the experiments at the modified GOL-3-II facility are presented. High-power electron beam (1MeV, 30kA, 8 µs) with the total energy content of up to 200 kJ heats the dense plasma in foilless regime in 12-m open trap with partly corrugated magnetic field. Stability of the beam-plasma system and improvement of plasma energy confinement are discussed.

articleTitle: Preparation of B4C thin film by pulsed ion-beam evaporation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Boron carbide (B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>C) is known as the material by its hardness, wear resistance and stability at high temperature. The preparation of thin film of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>C, therefore, is very important from the viewpoint of the industrial applications. We have experimentally tried to prepare thin film of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>C by using pulsed ion-beam evaporation (IBE), where high density ablation plasma is produced by the intense pulsed ion beam interaction with target. The crystallized B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>C thin films could be successfully deposited on Si (100) substrate by the front side deposition. Absorptions associated with the B-C combination and the vibration of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> - B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> clusters could be observed by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. Vickers hardness of the film deposited by front side deposition was observed to be HV∼1800.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation for generation of Carbon Simple Cubic by dynamic compression
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We proposed a sandwich structure target to achieve low entropy dynamic compression of diamond. The suitable condition to generate Carbon Simple Cubic are found by using the one-dimensional lagrangian hydrodynamics code and the tabulated equation of state.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic radiation generator for electromagnetic compatibility tests
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The present paper describes a powerful electromagnetic radiation generator designed for tests of radioelectron systems for electromagnetic compatibility over the range of frequencies from unities of kilohertz to 65 MHz and energies from several millijoules to 1 kJ and over.

articleTitle: Long term characteristics of repetitively operated high-current pulsed discharge gap switches
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Characteristics of repetitively operated high-current discharge gap switches are investigated to develop long life, high-repetition pulsed power switches. The discharge gap switches of gap length 4 mm were filled with 0.6 atm of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>, 3 atm of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> to obtain the initial self breakdown voltage around 20 kV. The switches are of pulsed discharged at peak current about 9 kA, duration about 400 ns with repetition rate of about 3 Hz. The breakdown voltages (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>) are recorded for 10,000 shots of discharge. From the experiment, we found that V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> and the scattering of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> increases with increasing the shots when using SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>. In contrast V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> and the scattering of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf> are almost constant when using H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. After the shot the discharge gas are analyzed and found that new composites were produced when using SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> where no new composite was observed when using H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas.

articleTitle: Characteristics of multichannel arc gap
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The characteristics of multichannel arc gap are investigated experimentally. The gap comprises 12 or 24 steel needle electrodes and a brass rod electrode. We examined the characteristics of the number of arc channels when the parameters below were changed: (a) rising rate of voltage pulse applied to the gap (b) length of feeders which transmit voltage pulse from the ferrite sharpener to each needle electrode (c) gap length (d) kind and pressure of inter-gap gas (e) with and without ultraviolet irradiation.

articleTitle: Pulsed Power: Sandia's plans for the new millennium
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Pulsed power science and engineering activities at Sandia National Laboratories grew out of a programmatic need for intense radiation sources to advance capabilities in radiographic imaging and to create environments for testing and certifying the hardness of components and systems to radiation in hostile environments. By the early 1970s, scientists in laboratories around the world began utilizing pulsed power drivers with very short (10s of nanoseconds) pulse lengths for Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF) experiments. In the United States, Defense Programs within the Department of Energy has sponsored this research. Recent progress in pulsed power, specifically fast-pulsed-power-driven z pinches, in creating temperatures relevant to ICF has been remarkable. Worldwide developments in pulsed power technologies and increased applications in both defense and industry are contrasted with ever increasing stress on research and development funding. The current environment has prompted us at Sandia to evaluate our role in the continued development of pulsed power science and to consider options for the future. This presentation will highlight our recent progress and provide an overview of our plans as we begin the new millennium.

articleTitle: Experimental operation of a z-pinch using a double gas puff
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report on the experimental operation of an argon double gas puff. The experiments were performed on the 200 ns, 4 MA Double-EAGLE facility at Maxwell Physics International. Extensive diagnostics demonstrated good quality implosions comparable in quality to short pulse (∼100 ns) z-pinches.

articleTitle: Study of the CVI 18.2nm line in a capillary discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Aiming at the development of short wavelength (XUV or soft X-ray) laser devices of the tabletop size, characteristics of a capillary tube discharge are examined. Time-integrated XUV spectra are analyzed with a flat-field grazing-incidence spectrometer equipped with a 1200 line/mm grating. The spatial distribution of the 18.2-nm transition intensity of CVI and its dependence on the discharge parameters such as the capillary length, the diameter and the discharge voltage are discussed.

articleTitle: Diagnostics of spatial structure of high-power E-beam by optical method
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Method of space-resolving calorimetry of a high-power electron beam has been developed. Picture of thermal radiation from front surface of the beam receiver is taken by absolutely calibrated CCD detector in visible and near IR range and then transformed into spatial distribution of the beam energy deposition into target. The method is particulary useful under high loads (∼1 kJ/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> energy density), up to regimes with noticeable erosion of the beam receiver.

articleTitle: Formation of DLC by a pure carbon arc under high vacuum
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The plasma of arc discharge of solid carbon has been applied to the formation of hard carbon thin films. A double-mesh electrode is placed at the exit of the sharply directed arc plasma column confined in the magnetic bottle. The RF voltage applied to the electrode is effective to diverge the plasma column radially to form a uniform plasma in front of the substrate and also to remove macroparticles. The characteristics of the obtained film are examined by Raman spectra, etc.

articleTitle: Injected electron acceleration by laser wakefield due to intense ultra-short laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The self-modulation of laser pulse shape, wakefield generation, and electron acceleration are investigated with a two dimensional electromagnetic wave propagation code and one and two dimensional fully relativistic electromagnetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation codes, which include optical field ionization. The generation mechanisms of the electric field in a recent experiment involving ultra-high-energy laser wakefield acceleration of injected electrons, by a laser pulse focused in a gas filled chamber are proposed.

articleTitle: Cleaning air from volatile organic compounds by pulsed electron beams
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Use of electron beams is effected for cleaning air from volatile organic compounds containing double C-C bound. On an example of styrene and ?crolein the researches of concentration dependencies of removal processes were carried out. Equations of energy distribution for process systematization of air cleaning by air-ionization methods are under consideration.

articleTitle: Laser light scattering diagnostics of high-pressure microgap discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A preliminary study of a microgap discharge aiming at CW excimer laser medium was carried out. Stable CW glow discharge was produced between knife-edge electrodes separated by ∼100 µm in atmospheric air by microwave (2.45 GHz) excitation. The plasma in the microgap was investigated by laser light scattering. A special triple-grating spectrometer with sharp notch characteristics for eliminating Rayleigh and stray scattering components was employed. When the discharge was absent, clear rotational Raman scattering due mainly to N2 molecules was observed; however, it almost disappeared when the discharge was turned on, indicating a high gas temperature (>∼3000 K) in the microgap. At a microwave power of 100 W, Thomson scattering signal was below a noise level, suggesting a electron density of <∼2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>.

articleTitle: Short microwave pulse generation by laser plasma in Utsunomiya university
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Short microwave pulse generation by the laser plasma in Utsunomiya University is presented. We are using two methods; one is called DARC(DC to AC Radiation Converter) which uses interaction between a periodic electrostatic wave and laser created ionization front propagating speed of light. Another is pulse slicing by the laser created overdense plasma in the waveguide. In the both experiments, we observed short microwave pulses of the order of nano second.

articleTitle: Simulation of metal surface heating caused by intense pulsed ion beam irradiation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We calculated a temperature rise of the target caused by an intense pulsed ion beam irradiation numerically. When a proton beam with 200 keV, 420 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 60 nsec is irradiated to a pure titanium target, the temperature of surface region within 2.3 µm is increased above its melting point. The maximum cooling rate is reached to 1.3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> K/sec. This value is sufficiently larger than the critical cooling rate for amorphous formation of pure titanium.

articleTitle: Dielectric/gas interface breakdown caused by high power microwaves
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Physical mechanisms leading to microwave breakdown on dielectric/gas interfaces are investigated for power density on the order of 10 MW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at 2.85 GHz and gas pressures on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> torr to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> torr. The investigation is focused on an alumina/air interface; other gases are considered for reference purposes. A 3 MW magnetron with 3.5 µs pulse width is coupled to an S-band traveling wave resonator with a pressure adjustable test region. The pre-breakdown phase and the breakdown are monitored by recording the traveling and reflected power, and the spatially integrated luminosity. Electric field probes in the vicinity of the interface are included as well to get information about the local field. Furthermore, the light emission was observed with an image intensifier capable of a minimum gate time of 2.5 ns, in temporal correlation to the other phenomena, or with a framing camera having a 20 ns gate time and 100 ns separation between pictures. The pressure dependent breakdown characteristics, such as appearance, breakdown field, and temporal shape of electric signals, are compared to dielectric/vacuum interface breakdown and volume breakdown, all measured utilizing similar setups.

articleTitle: Novel large-area high-resolution-transmission-electron-microscopy technique using FIB-fabricated specimens
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A novel LA-HRTEM specimen fabrication technique using an FIB apparatus was developed. Using this technique, cation composition in a K-Al-Si-Sn-Ti-Zr-O specimen was performed by EDS. The cation composition of regions located more than 200 nm apart from the interface between a ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> grain and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> matrix was same as that in ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. This indicates that the accuracy of EDS analyses in the LA-HRTEM specimens was confirmed.

articleTitle: Response of converters to heating by intense heavy ion beams
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The high current upgrade of the accelerator facilities at GSI Darmstadt, Germany, has created possibilities for a new class of experiments with heavy ion beams. Intense pulses of heavy ion beams can rapidly heat converters to high temperatures. The energy deposition of heavy ion beams as well as the hydrodynamic response of the converters and the radiation emitted from the converters are investigated experimentally.

articleTitle: Plasma containers made from high-Tc superconducting tubes (supertrons)
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Pulsed neon plasma was produced at 0.2 and 1.0 Torr in the bore of a high-critical temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>) bismuth-based sintered superconductor tube (supertron) with a T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> of ∼l03 K. The tube had a 9-mm inner diameter, a 1.5-mm-thick wall, and a 60-mm axial length. The discharge electrodes were separated by 32 mm. Spatiotemporal behaviors of the plasma were observed using a streak camera through an imaging fiber. The experimental results showed that the superconducting tube contained the plasma more effectively than the normal conducting one.

articleTitle: Nanosecond and subnanosecond generation of intense electron beams through high-Tc superconducting tubes (supertrons)
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In previous experiments, a double-layered high-T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> supercon-ducting tube (supertron) consisting of an inner bismuth-based powder-pressed pipe and an outer yttrium-based melt-processed pipe easily generated intense electron beams with a duration of 1.5 ns at 80 K. Based on a model for this pulse compression, we examined another modified double-layered tube to generate shorter pulses. The shortest pulse obtained, 2.4 ns at 70 K, demanded further modification to the configuration of the supertron to realize subnanosecond pulses.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of foil acceleration by intense pulsed ion beam
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: When we irradiate an intense pulsed ion beam to a foil, ablation plasma is created, and the foil is accelerated. In this paper, we developed a numerical model of this phenomenon. We analyze temperature and pressure of the ablation plasma, and velocity of the accelerated foil by the numerical simulation. It was possible for us to analyze a behavior and detailed results of the ablation plasma expansion and acceleration of the foil. We could also observe the processes of the ablation plasma expansion and acceleration of the foil by the back lighting high-speed photography. The calculated results of foil velocity agree well with experimental ones over the wide range of energy density of an ion beam. We analyzed time trend of the foil velocity. And we could see that the foil is rapidly accelerated just after delay.

articleTitle: Generation of sub-picosecond GeV electron bunches by laser acceleration in vacuum
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The interaction of free electrons with intense laser beams in vacuum was studied using 3D test particle simulation instead of solving analytically the relativistic Newton-Lorentz equation of motions. We found a group of solutions of the equation which show very interesting and unusual characteristics. When the laser intensity is strong enough a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ≥100, where a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ≡ eE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> / m<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>ωc is a measure of the laser intensity, an electron can be captured into the high-intensity region and accelerated to GeV energy with acceleration gradient of tens of GeV/cm. The accelerated GeV electron bunch is a macro-pulse composed of a lot of micro-pulses. The paraxial approximation equations of the Gaussian laser beam used in the simulation are of high accuracy and the contribution of the high-order correction is almost negligible when the laser beam width w<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ≥ 60.

articleTitle: NOx reduction using combined system of pulse corona with catalyst
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this work we report the NOx removal by reduction using two types of plasma reactors; the plasma-driven catalyst (PDC) reactor and the plasma-enhanced selective catalytic reduction (PE-SCR) reactor. In the PDC system, reduction was found to be the dominant pathway of NOx removal under the presence of additives. Gas hourly space velocity (GHSV) and type of additives were found to be important parameters which determine the removal rates of NO and NOx in the PDC system. In the PE-SCR system with NH3, the plasma converted most of NO to NO2, and total NOx was successfully reduced over the Co-ZSM5 catalyst.

articleTitle: Analysis of the pulsed plasma reactor impedance for DeSOx and DeNOx
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The impedance characteristics of the wire-plate pulsed plasma reactor for deSO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> and deNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> were investigated by experiment. The impedance characteristics of the reactor were mainly varied with charge voltage, wire length and wire-plate distance. In addition, we performed an analysis of the nonlinear reactor impedance on the basis of experiment and EMTP work.

articleTitle: Design of a system for conversion of the output of frequency tunable gyrotron into a Gaussian beam
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper we present a novel design of two quasi-optical systems for conversion of gyrotron outputs into gaussian beams. They consist of a quasi-optical antenna, focusing mirrors and a filter which removes the side lobes of the beam. One is capable to convert three TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1n</inf> mode outputs into Gaussian beams and the other is capable to convert three TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</inf> mode outputs into Gaussian beams.

articleTitle: Effect of pulse width on NOx removal using non-thermal plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Non-thermal plasmas generated by pulsed power have been widely used in many applications. This produces high-energy electrons, which contribute to many plasma chemical reactions, and those reactions have been used to remove NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, VOC and dioxin.

articleTitle: High power microwave generation by a coaxial vircator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A coaxial-type virtual cathode oscillator (vircator) was tested in the Pulsed Power Laboratory at Texas Tech University with electron beam parameters of 500 kV, 40 kA, and 30 ns. The major goal of this experiment was to understand the characteristics of the coaxial vircator and the effect of the feedback field on the microwave efficiency. The experimental results have given the output microwave power of ∼ 400 MW, the microwave energy efficiency of ∼ 2 %, the microwave frequency of ∼ 2 GHz, and the microwave mode of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> in circular waveguide. By enhancing the field intensity around the vircator using a microwave reflector, the microwave output power was increased to ∼ 900 MW giving microwave energy efficiency of ∼ 5.5 %. This efficiency is calculated as peak microwave power divided by peak beam power, which does not occur at the same time. The instantaneous efficiency, using the beam power at the time of the peak microwave power is 20%.

articleTitle: Development of large size ion source for ion Shower Doping
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We developed the new Ion Shower Doping system “ISDR series” for formation of TFTS. This system is available for large glass substrate of 680 × 880 mm maximumly. We simplify the glass transform system, so glass move only horizontally. Beam uniformity achieve 2 to 3% (3σ). We introduce here the property of new ISDR series comparing with conventional ISD series.

articleTitle: Effect of backscattered electrons on the thermal conditions of the target under electron-beam treatment
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It has been shown that on irradiation of a target by an electron beam formed in a direct-action diode and transported toward the target by a guide magnetic field an important role is played by the electrons multiply reflected from the target. The Monte Carlo method was used to investigate how these electrons returning to the target after their reflection in the acceleration region affect the distribution of the energy absorbed in the target and the spectrum of the electrons incident on the target. An algorithm has been proposed to calculate these characteristics based on the method for resolution of the electron flow by its intersections with the target-vacuum interface.

articleTitle: The status of 17 GHz gyroklystron program at university of maryland
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: 80 MW Ku-band gyroklytrons are being developed with pulse duration of one microsecond for driving future linear colliders. Three- and four-cavity coaxial schemes are presented in this paper. Numerical simulations predict efficiency over 32%, with 50–60dB gain, and 80 MW power level for gyroklystrons operating at second harmonic (17.136GHz). It is shown that a four-cavity circuit could improve significantly the gain and reduce the power of the driving source.

articleTitle: Internal electric field formation in insulators under high-flux negative ion implantation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Ion-flux dependent nanoparticle formation is observed in silica glasses under high-flux 60 keV Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup> implantation. Under the high-flux implantation, a strong electric field possibly forms in the glass, and may affect the nanoparticle formation via the solute diffusion processes. In this paper, the internal-field formation is evaluated based on a model for negative ion implantation, in which different diffusion lengths of electrons and holes cause the field. The calculated fields sustain more than 2000 nm in depth, although the ion range is less than 100 nm. The fields hardly depend on the ion flux and the maximum value is 3.3 kV/cm. Mechanism to create the internal field and a possibility of high flux effects are discussed.

articleTitle: Generation of high current pulsed heavy ion beams using bi-directionaol pulses
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Intense pulsed heavy ion beams (PHIB) of carbon, nitrogen, aluminum, etc., have a wide area of applications including nuclear fusion, materials science, etc. To produce a pure PHIB a new type of pulsed power ion accelerator is proposed. The accelerator consists of two acceleration gaps (an ion source gap and a post acceleration gap) and a drift tube and a bi-directional pulse is used to accelerate the ions. The concept of the accelerator is described with the principle to remove impurities. In addition, two types of pulse forming lines are proposed to generate bi-directional pulses for the accelerator. In the experiment, the bi-directional pulses of negative and positive pulse of duration 50 ns each are successfully generated by the proposed pulse forming lines.

articleTitle: Compact proton accelerator utilizing an intense laser
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>× B acceleration scheme or surfatron has an advantage for protons and/or ions acceleration in case of the phase matching between the electromagnetic wave and these particles. A new proton accelerator utilizing the transverse electric field of the laser wakefield is proposed. In the proton acceleration employing the transverse laser wakefield, we have performed the simulation. The results show that the energy gain per one stage is not large enough but the acceleration gradient is several hundred times larger than the conventional proton acceleration scheme. The proton acceleration by the transverse wakefield is more effective in lower proton energy. It will be possible to make the compact proton accelerator with these principles.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of excitation of electromagnetic waves by electron beam in partially filled plasma waveguide
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this work the process of electromagnetic radiation (EMR) excitation by an electron beam is also investigated in the case of the plasma waveguides where the plasma density varies along the system according to the periodic (harmonic) 1aw. In the examined system the plasma wave is synchronous with the beam. The plasma wave is parametrically coupled with the fast electromagnetic wave (EMW) propagating in the vacuum gap between the plasma boundary and the conductive jacket. The coupling is stimulated by the plasma density periodic inhomogeneity. It's demonstrated that in this system the process of the plasma wave parametric transformation into EMR stimulates increase of efficiency of the power pumpover from the electron beam.

articleTitle: Simulation of the high-power electron beam formation and recuperation designed for ion source
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This work shows the result of the numerical simulation of the Electron Optic System (EOS), which must be used for the formation and transportation of the high-power electron beam from a long channel. The modeling was taken of the program, which based by using the finite difference non-iniform nets and the model beam from the deformable elements. EOS' main parameters were following. The electron gun forming of the beams with the perveance is 1,5 A/V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/2</sup>, coefficient of the compress is 200 and the electron beam density is 2,6·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.The magnetic system is create of the special distribution magnetic field of 2000 Gs, which give at addition compression of the beam and transport from the long channel of length 1 meter with minimal pulsations. The collector is use recuperation regime 0,07 U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> for the high economical efficiency.

articleTitle: Pulsed ion-beam evaporation for thin film deposition
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The process of pulsed ion-beam evaporation was studied by investigating its three important parts: target ablation, plasma expansion, and thin-film deposition. The diagnostic results have shown that the target mass loss caused by ion beam ablation mainly depends on the melting and boiling temperatures of the target materials. In addition, high-speed photographs have shown that the expansion of the ablation plasma is well directional. The result of the thin-film composition analysis has indicated that the ablation plasma moved along the substrate surface during the thin film deposition.

articleTitle: Free electron laser and advanced light source studies on electron storage ring and Linac at LASTI
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Free electron laser and advanced light source studies are started on the “NewSUBARU”, a 1.5 GeV synchrotron radiation facility, and on the “LEENA”, a Laser Emitted ElectroN Accelerator (15 MeV Linac) at LASTI. NewSUBARU will be used not only as soft x-ray synchrotron radiation sources for various application but also to study a coherent x-ray generation, a γ-ray generation by laser-Compton back scattering and an ultra-short pulse x-ray generation. Preliminary experiments on LEENA with < 6MeV operation shows a far infrared (wavelength of 65 to 75 µm) generation. Newly developing photo cathode RF gun using needle cathode are studied for improve the output power of FEL and expand the operation wavelength from 10µm to 100µm on LEENA.

articleTitle: NOx treatment by atmospheric streamer corona discharges
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Among many methods used for removal of NOx from flue gas, a positive DC streamer corona discharge method is presented in this paper. To generate a uniform streamer corona discharge with simplified DC power supplies, a series gap was connecting with the main discharge reactor. When the series gap operated, a voltage pulse whose dv/dt was from 0.7kV/ns to 2.72kV/ns (according to the gap space) was applied on the main reactor. The electrical and optical measurements showed that the series gap was useful for obtaining the uniform discharge. The energy consumption of series gap was about from 6% to 20% of the discharge input power for different series gap space of 0.3mm to 1.05mm. Until now the maximum NO removal rate of 67.7% was obtained at the main gap spacing of 30mm and series gap spacing of 0.9mm. Maximum removal efficiency of 3.52gNO/kWh was also obtained at the series gap spacing of 0.3mm.
