articleTitle: Study of the gas puff on wire array implosion
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This report is devoted to the structured Z-pinch with long time implosion. Experiments were carried out on GIT 12 inductive storage. In the experiment with an outer gas puff and an inner wire array, we have been able to attain efficient switching of the current on a level of 2.1 MA into the wire array. The total implosion time was 300 ns, while the time of implosion of the wire array was not over 100 ns. The final velocity of the wire array was 5·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> cm/s. The switching occurs owing to the anomalous resistance appearing in the outer gas puff when heavy gases (krypton and xenon) with small masses are used for the gas puff material.

articleTitle: Kα emission from high-Z solids irradiated by intense femtosecond laser pulses
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have investigated the X-ray emission from a solid target irradiated by an intense ultra short pulse laser using computer codes. We have combined the plasma hydrodynamics code, PIC code and Monte-Carlo code for the emission of X-ray from the solid target. This unique approach allows us to make an estimation of the energy distribution of the hot electrons produced during the interaction of the laser and pre-plasma, which determines the X-ray spectrum and conversion efficiency. The calculated result is found to agree with experimental X-ray emission from the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 42 fs laser irradiated Cu target.

articleTitle: Multi-layer carbon nitride thin films prepared by repeated process of carbon sputter-deposition and nitrogen ion implantation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Multi-layer carbon nitride (CN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) films have been deposited onto Si (100) substrates by repeated process of DC magnetron sputter-deposition and nitrogen ion beam (N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>) implantation. The composition, bonding structure and mechanical properties of multi-layer CN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films prepared by the repeated process were investigated. Depth profile studies by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) showed that it is possible to control the layer structure by regulating sputter deposition time and ion beam energy in the repeated process. Two different films were fabricated and compared. The one is a multi-layer film of carbon and carbon nitride and the other is a homogeneous layer film of carbon nitride. Measurements of internal stress of the films showed compression. Variation in the morphology of multi-layer CN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films and non-irradiated CN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> film deposited by pure N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas sputtering was examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Nanoindentation studies revealed that the hardness of multi-layer CN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> films was higher than that of non-irradiated CN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> film.

articleTitle: Luminescent properties of SrAl2O4:Eu thin films deposited by intense pulsed ion-beam evaporration
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: SrAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> activated with Eu, one of long phosphorescent materials with high brightness, has been successfully deposited on Si substrates using the intense pulsed ion-beam evaporation. The prepared SrAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Eu thin films had a polycrystalline structure without annealing and showed a typical photoluminescence of SrAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Eu at around 520 nm. The thermoluminescence (TL) measurements were carried out in order to obtain the lifetimes of the phosphorescence. Especially, TL spectra in the higher temperature region, which contributed for the long phosphorescence, were examined by the partial heating technique to evaluate the distributed trap depths and the lifetimes. The lifetime at 300 K for the prepared film was found to be about 180 min.

articleTitle: Generation and amplification of powerful ultrashort microwave pulses
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental results of the observation of superradiance from intense, subnanosecond electron bunches moving through a periodic waveguide and interacting with a backward propagating TM01 wave are presented. At 38 GHz 60 MW 300 ps pulses were generated by 200 keV, 1.2 kA, 1 ns electron bunch. The SR pulse power increased up to 150 MW when electron energy and current were increase up to 300 keV and 2 kA. The initial observation of 75 GHz 10–15 MW radiation pulses with duration less than 150 ps, and of 150 GHz microwave spikes with a risetime of 75 ps are also reported. The ultra-short microwave pulses in Ka, W, and G band were generated with repetition frequencies of up to 25 Hz. It is demonstrated the possibility of further amplification and shortening of SR pulses during propagation of these pulses over quasi continues electron beam.

articleTitle: Plasma emission sources for intense electron beams
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Various sources are being used for generation of high-current electron beams (current amplitude of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>A, electron energy of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup>eV and pulse duration of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup>s) in specially designed diodes. The main requirements for these sources are as follows: (a) electron emission occurs simultaneously with the accelerating pulse; (b) the extracted electron current density should be governed by the space-charge law; (c) the extracted electron current density should be uniform in its cross-section; (d) the electron source should have a long lifetime (≥10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> pulses) and it has to be reliable and reproducible; (e) the electron source should be compatible for operation in vacuum of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup>Torr. One can divide electron sources into passive and active ones. By passive sources we consider sources which emit electrons under the application of an accelerating pulse. By active sources we consider sources of plasma that can be produced by various methods prior to the application of the accelerating pulse. In this review we consider different types of passive cathodes operating at E≤10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>V/cm and active plasma sources based on ferroelectric cathodes.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of ignition perspectives at gas-dynamical compression of capsule with DT gas by high-speed plasma liner
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Numerical investigations of ignition perspectives at gas-dynamical capsule compression with DT gas are presented in this paper. Semi-empiric parameters of accelerated liner, determined with analysis of experiments on x-ray radiation generation on PBFA-Z facility are used. Results of one-dimensional scaling calculations of neutron output, temperature and gas compression for wide range of current values of liner system are presented. Prognosis for EMIR facility are made.

Author Keywords: gas-dynamical capsule compression with DT gas

articleTitle: Ferroelectric plasma cathodes
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We present results of studies of charged particle and light emission from ferroelectric plasma cathodes. Results of lifetime tests of different ferroelectric cathodes are also described. We studied the operation of a planar electron diode with ferroelectric cathodes having emitting areas of 10cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 100cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> under the application of a high-voltage pulse of 25kV and 300kV, respectively, with a repetition rate ≤5Hz. Data related to the uniformity of the extracted electron beam, the potential distribution, impedance, power, and energy of the diode operating with these cathodes are given as well. We also present data of the vacuum deterioration as a result of cathode operation.

articleTitle: Smid code for studying physical processes in magnetic self-insulation diodes
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We present a Solver for Magnetic Self-Insulation Diodes (SMID) Code, developed for studies on high-current relativistic diodes, and supply examples of its applied usage. In order to analyze experimental data and numerical simulation results an in-circuit approach has been developed with an appropriate theory elaborated.

articleTitle: Measurement of IREB-driven strong langmuir field using electron beam probing technique
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Application of electron beam probing technique to clarify the existence of the caviton has been studied. In this paper analytical and numerical analyses are given on the deflection patterns of the probe beam passing through a caviton. Also results of a previous experiment are discussed on the basis of these analyses.

articleTitle: Development of frequency-tunable free-electron maser for feeding high-gradient accelerating structures
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new type of a high selective Bragg resonator having a step of corrugation inside the interaction region was used as a microwave system for a free-electron maser (FEM). Using a linac LIU-3000 to drive the FEM-oscillator a single-mode single-frequency operation was achieved at a frequency of 30.74 GHz with an output power of about 50 MW, which corresponded to a record efficiency of 35% for a millimeter wavelength FEM.

articleTitle: 200MW reletivistic backward-wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The design and experimental results of a X-band relativistic high-power backward-wave oscillator driven by a 1 MV linear induction accelerator is presented. The design includes a linear numerical analysis and the simulations using the 2_-dimension electromagnetic particle-in-cell MAGIC code. Peak output power of about 210 MW was generated with frequency of 9.8 GHz and duration time of 50 ns. This pulsed microwave radiation will be used to drive a GW order high-power free-electro laser amplifier.

articleTitle: Modification of metal surface by direct ion implantation from a nitrogen plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Nitrogen ions were implanted into an aluminum alloy (Al-7Si) for casting mold materials by plasma-based ion implantation. The AES analysis of ion-implanted Al-7Si indicated that the depth profile of implanted nitrogen ions was approximated by a Gaussian, and that the AlN layer was formed by nitrogen-ion-implantation. The tribological test showed the reduction of friction coefficient from 0.60 to 0.12 and the improvement of wear resistance by nitrogen-ion implantation. The oxide resistance of the nitrogen-implanted sample was also enhanced.

articleTitle: Thermal stresses and microstructural transformations in thin copper samples irradiated with a high-current electron beam
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Irradiation of metals and alloys by pulsed electron beams modifies their structure and properties. When irradiating a copper foil with a high-current electron beam of energy ∼20 keV, power density ∼10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and pulse duration 50 ns, we observed microtwins in the near-surface region of the target, testifying to the fact that the loading was high-speed in character and the peak pressure was over an order of magnitude higher than the dynamic yield stress. However, calculations have shown that the amplitude of the compression-rarefaction pulse was not over 2 MPa, which is below the dynamic yield stress by two orders of magnitude. To explain these results, we have calculated thermal stresses in terms of the theory of thermal deformation of thin plates. The calculations have shown that these stresses reach 3 GPa in magnitude at the target surface. The stresses relax with equalization of the temperature (the equalization time is ∼10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> s for a copper sample). The stress magnitude is consistent with experiments on determination of the threshold for twinning in copper foils under shock-wave loading.

articleTitle: State of the art of the theory of relativistic plasma microwave electronics
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Theoretical research on high-power microwave sources based on stimulated emission from relativistic election beams (REBs) in plasma waveguides are reviewed. Both microwave amplifiers and oscillators are investigated. Two mechanisms for stimulated resonant Cherenkov emission from a relativistic electron beam — single-particle or Thomson emission and collective or Raman emission — are studied. Although the paper is devoted to theoretical problems, all estimates and are made with real experiments in mind and theoretical results are compared with experimental data.

articleTitle: Beam-nonuniformity smoothing using density valley formed by ion beam deposition in an ICF fuel pellet
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We study the beam non-uniformity smoothing effect of the radiation transport in the density valley formed by an ion-beam deposition in a heavy ion-beam inertial confinement fusion pellet by numerical simulations. The simulation results show that the radiation energy is confined in the density valley, and the beam non-uniformity can be smoothed out by the radiation transport along the density valley. In addition, an estimation for the Rayleigh-Taylor instability growth during the implosion phase is also presented.

articleTitle: Transport efficiency of intense relativistic electron beam in pre-formed plasma channel
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Relativistic electron beam (REB: 300keV, 5kA, 60ns) transport efficiency has been investigated by injecting the REB into a preformed argon plasma channel in the drift tube. Transport efficiency has been obtained from two Rogowski coils separated by 20cm each other. At the vacuum drift tube, the transport efficiency is about 20%, in which the propagation beam current is below the space charge limiting current. It is found that the transport efficiency could be increased up to 48% when the pre-formed plasma channel density is 1.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>, which is close to that of REB.

articleTitle: Constructing the six-dimensional Vlasov solver using Constrained Interpolation Profile scheme
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new numerical scheme for solving the hyper-dimensional Vlasov equation in phase space is proposed. At each time step, the distribution function and its first derivatives are advected in phase space by the Constrained Interpolation Profile (CIP) scheme. Although a cell within grid points is interpolated by a cubic-polynomial, any matrix solutions are not required. The scheme guarantees the exact conservation of the mass. Even if we reduce the number of grid points in v-direction, the scheme still give the stable, accurate and reasonable results with memory storage comparable to particle simulations. Owing to this fact, the scheme has succeeded to be generalized in a straightforward way to deal with the six-dimensional, or full-dimensional problems.

articleTitle: Computer simulation of axis-encircling beams generated by electron gun with permanent magnet system
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results from numerical simulations of a novel electron gun which forms axis-encircling electron beams with small velocity spread and ripple are presented and discussed. It utilizes magnetic system based on NdFeB permanent magnet. The parameters of generated beams are appropriate for a prospective compact, mildly relativistic large-orbit gyrotron (LOG) whose development is in progress at the Research Center for Development of Far-Infrared Region in Fukui University.

articleTitle: Design considerations for the JAERI industrial 1.3micron 40kW highly-efficient FEL driven by the superconducting rf linac
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: As the JAERI superconducting rf linac based free-electron laser (FEL) has successfully been lased to produce a 2.34kW FEL light and 100kW electron beam output in quasi continuous wave(qCW) operation recently, it exceeded twice of the 1kW program goal. As our next program goal, a 40 kW FEL light and 4 MW electron beam output in qCW operation is planned in the JAERI superconducting rf linac based FEL facility. Conceptual design considerations needed for such a very high power operation will be discussed to improve the existing facility.

articleTitle: Influence of the surface-roughness of dielectric electrode on ozone generation in a silent discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Influence of surface roughness of dielectric electrode on high-density ozone generation is investigated. Tempax<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> glass and alumina ceramics are used as dielectrics. Average values of surface roughness of glass plate are varied from 0.004 µm to 6.6 µm, and these of alumina ceramics are varied from 0.045 µm to 7.0 µm. Ozone generation efficiency with a rough-surface plate is lower than that with a smooth-surface one. The efficiency reduction should be caused by the surface roughness that limits the growth of surface discharge.

articleTitle: Imaging XUV monochromator on base of spherical multilayer mirror
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The using of curved multilayer mirrors in XUV spectroscopy opens new possibilities for the measurement of spatial line emission profiles and impurity transport parameters in high temperature plasma.

articleTitle: Development of 3-D simulation model for laser material processing
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Laser welding is one of the most important fields of laser material processing. In this study, we discuss the outline of 3-D simulation model of the laser welding and experiments for validation. The availability of the present model was confirmed to compare the results of experiments with numerical analysis in the range of lower laser energy intensity.

articleTitle: Conceptional design of the pulsed electron beam facility GESA II
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The new pulsed electron beam facility GESA-2 designed for material surface treatment is described in the report. The feature of this facility, in comparison to the first one - GESA-1, is the possibility to realize larger melted depths (∼ 100 µm), which are required for many applications. Parameters of electron beam being produced are: electron energy 200 - 400 keV; beam current 200 – 400 A; beam cross-section 50 – 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>; pulse duration 5 – 250 µs; maximum power density at the target 6 MW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>; maximum energy density 500 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. All beam parameters are controlled. Main parts of the facility are described, results of beam parameters measurements are presented.

articleTitle: Side extraction type secondary emission electron gun using wire ion plasma source
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A secondary emission electron gun applicable for gas treatment was designed, fabricated and tested. The gun is set beside an ion source, which is called a wire ion plasma source (WIPS). Ions extracted from WIPS are accelerated toward the cathode surface, which is set oblique to the ion loci. By collision of ions, secondary electrons emitted from this cathode surface are then accelerated toward the electron window and form a very wide electron beam. The electron window is set orthogonal to the ion extraction window and is on earth potential. In order to inject the electron beam perpendicular to the electron window, the ion and electron trajectories were numerically simulated for several conditions. A wide electron beam current distribution inside the gas treatment chamber was observed when a honeycomb board and an Al film were placed at the electron window. The electron beam current density of 6.4 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> measured at cathode voltage of 80 kV possess sufficient energy to irradiate gaseous pollutants like NOx.

articleTitle: Low pellet gain and high efficiency icf power plant model by MHD power generation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We propose a low pellet gain and high efficiency inertial confinement fusion (ICF) power generation system using a magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) power generation, and employ analytical comparative studies for power generation system options. When the thermal output at high temperature (about 2000–2400K) can be extracted from a fusion reactor, only an MHD generator can be used and can convert efficiently ICF output energy into electricity even under such a high temperature condition. In this study, we investigate on a high efficiency gas-cooled ICF power generation system using a non-equilibrium closed cycle MHD generator. As a result, it is found that the power generation efficiency of 65% can be achieved by using a simple MHD power generation without a bottoming cycle in a heavy ion ICF power plant. Additionally, the enhancement of power generation efficiency reduces the requirements for ICF technologies. Therefore, even lower pellet gain becomes acceptable when high efficiency ICF power plant can be established by using an MHD power generation system as shown in this study.

articleTitle: Intense-electron-beam transport control through an insulator beam collimator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper we present a new interesting physics in an intense-electron-beam transport control using an insulator collimator: the ion extraction from a plasma generated at the insulator surface is self-regulated by the net space charge of the electron beam in order for the effective charge neutralization. A part of beam electrons hits the insulator surface, and the electron charge accumulated at the insulator surface creates the local discharges. The discharges produce the plasma at the insulator surface. This paper also presents a plasma generation effect at the insulator guide surface on an intense-electron-beam transportation through the insulator beam guide. The ion extraction from the plasma is delayed by the plasma-generation time. The simulation results present that 1) the self-regulated space-charge neutralization, 2) the simplicity of the system, and 3) the head of the electron beam pulse is used to generate the plasma.

articleTitle: Computer simulation of forming and transportation of electron beam with discount own 3D magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The problem of self-focus of beams by their own magnetic fields was explored. Description of the mathematical model of 3D computer program for analysis of the multi-beam system are given. 7-beams on 120 A and 100 kV injector of electrons was investigated by program. Experimental results confirm the change of beam's profiles.

articleTitle: Propagation of intense pulsed proton beam through z-discharged plasma channel in the presence of return channels
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental studies are presented on the propagation of an intense, pulsed, proton beam (890 kV, 50 ns) through a z-discharged plasma channel (50 cm long, 1.1 ∼ 10 Torr, air) in the presence of return channels (30 cm long). Using a high-speed camera and a small-sized magnetic probe, we have found the compression (deformation) of the main channel due to the presence of the return channels. The enhancement of the beam power density has also been observed. Good efficiency of the propagation (∼ 33 %) has been observed through the main channel.

articleTitle: Measurements of density and velocity of sheath plasma from magneto-plasma-dynamic (MPD) gun
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The Magneto-plasma-dynamic (MPD) thruster has been investigated for next generation pollution-free engine for interplanetary travelling and position modification of the satellite, and it has been used for initial plasma generation at the magnetic mirror device. We have fabricated the MPD thruster, which has maximum 1 kV, 10 kA, and 1 ms pulse duration. And we have measured the density and temperature of sheath plasma from the thruster with Langmuir probe and double probe. Also propagation velocity of sheath plasma has been measured by optical probe.

articleTitle: Operation of high-power planar Fem with two-dimensional Bragg reflectors (theoretical and experimental investigations)
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Recent results of investigations on powerful 4-mm planar FEM driven by sheet electron beam in case of 2-D distributed feedback are described. Spectral properties of Bragg resonators and generated power together with its dependency on undulator field are measured for the various resonators. Obtained dependencies are in agreement with ones predicted by theoretical models. Power level and pulse duration are limited by microwave shortening in the experiments. Prospects of increasing of these parameters are discussed.

articleTitle: Thermal balance in plane thermoionic cathodes of radio-frequency tubes without anodes
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Cathode units of high power radio-frequency tubes are conventionally used in electron injectors with high repetition rate. This cathode utilization results in disturbance of the temperature regime of the cathode surface because of cutting the anode, which is “thermal mirror” in the tube. Estimations made in this work show an essential lowering of the emitter temperature for both porous metal and oxide cathodes without anodes. It shows that the oxide cathode utilization results in a significant thermal gradient in the oxide layer.

articleTitle: The primary studies of an improved vircator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experiment studies of a vircator with microwave feedback were conducted on the TM-01 REB accelerator. In the improved vircator scheme, the microwave generated by virtual cathode oscillation would be partially fed back to the beam acceleration region to modulate the e-beam current and so as to improve the performance of the vircator. It was found from the experiment that the radiated microwave power, which peaked up to 1.25GW, was related to the length of the feedback waveguide and had periodic character when the feedback waveguide length changed step by step. The experimental results were presents and a forced oscillation model was proposed to explain the experimental phenomena.

articleTitle: High performance Ni-Like soft-x-ray lasers by longitudinal-Pumping and transient collisional excitation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We experimentally investigate the interaction of a preformed plasma with a high intensity 2-psec Nd:Glass laser pulse entering from the longitudinal direction. Observations of the transverse intensity profile of the longitudinal beam are found to be well reproduced by simple hydrodynamic and ray-tracing calculations, if a nonuniform line-focus is taken into account. Observations of visible emission from the plasma reveal the presence of a bright jetlike structure, which extends over an unusually long length of several millimeters. This phenomenon is found to favor plasma produced from middle- to high-Z material.

articleTitle: Energy recuperator for sheet beam of magnetized electrons
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: For the electron beams in a guiding magnetic field with significant energy and angular spreads of the particles two novel schemes of recuperator with different configurations are described. In the first one a special combination of transversal and longitudinal magnetic fields is used to separate electrons due to different Larmour radii corresponded to different energy of their longitudinal motion. In the second variant of recuperator an essential new scheme of recuperator is suggested. Here a spatially periodic transverse magnetic field is added to the longitudinal one in the deceleration section of electron trajectory. A resonance between bounce electron motion and cyclotron one gives strong increasing of Larmour radius for a small group of electrons with chosen particle energy. As a result, the electrons with resonance energy fall out to small local parts of channel wall where collector plates are placed. Comparison of two schemes of the recuperator is also discussed.

articleTitle: Ferroelectric thin films prepared by backside pulsed ion-beam evaporation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Ferroelectric (PbTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> or Pb(Zr,Ti)O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) thin films have been successfully prepared on Si(100) or pyrex glasses by backside deposition of intense pulsed ion beam evaporation. The ion beam parameters were typically beam energy = 1.3 MeV, ion-current density on target = 0.7 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, pulse duration = 50 ns. The composition of the thin films was good agreement with that of the original target. The relative dielectric constant at 1 kHz was obtained to be 20, while that by normal front side deposition was 150.

articleTitle: Study of imploding plasmas on the S-300 machine
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The successful experiment carried out the last years on “Z” and “ANGARA-5” facilities on soft X-ray generation in wire-arrays implosion attract much attention. On “S-300” generator (700 kV, 4 MA, 70 ns) the experimental studies are also carried on with wire-array output units to create a powerful X-ray source. The development of more new diagnostic methods will definitely contribute to attain new data which could help in explanation of a X-ray emission mechanism of imploding multi-wire arrays that is not yet well understood.

articleTitle: An application of an intense pulsed ion beam to metal surface modifications
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A pure titanium and a high-speed tool steel (SKH51) are irradiated by an intense pulsed ion beam (IPIB) with the ion energy of 180 keV, the ion current density of 460 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the pulse duration of 65 ns. A nanocrystalline structure of pure titanium is formed on the surface by IPIB-irradiation, resulting in an enhancement of wear resistance. By IPIB irradiation to the SKH51, the second phase carbides of VC, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>C, and Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>C are dispersed from the surface. A high-temperature phase, austenite, composed of nm-sized polycrystals is produced on the SKH51 surface by the repeated irradiation of IPIB.

articleTitle: Calculation of ion beam sputtering yield of solid sample with cylindrical cavities on its surface
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Analytical expressions which determine the fraction of sputtered atoms escaping from a cylindrical cavity on the target surface bombarded by an ion beam are obtained for their cosine and over-cosine angle distributions. It is shown that the sputtering yield can be substantially reduced by creation a relief of cylindrical cavities on the sputtered surface.

articleTitle: Development of 1MV steep-front and longduration square impulse voltage generator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The basic design and performance of a newly developed 1MV steep-front and long-duration square impulse voltage generator, named “SPARK”, are described. Advanced pulsed-power technology and elaborate circuit design enable an ideal square impulse voltage waveform, in which the rise time of the wavefront is shorter than 20ns and a long flat-topped voltage crest continues up to 10µs, to be generated. Experimental results of sparkover voltage and time (V-t) characteristics in SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas measured using “SPARK” are also presented.

articleTitle: About some characteristics and industrial application of ion beams generated in an abnormal glow discharge with a liquid dielectric anode
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Feasibility of generating ion beams with energy of keV and high enough density (more than 1mA per cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) in abnormal glow discharges has been previously based physically. The results of investigations of radial distribution of the ion beam density with the help of a designed polycylindrical collector are presented. The features of the current density distribution for a single and multipoint current input-emitter are discussed.

articleTitle: Subnanosecond pulse electron-beam driver for the microtron-recuperator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The problem of generating short pulses of electron current for injection into accelerator exists. Devices built around by traditional methods cannot generate pulses of electron current shorter than 1 ns with amplitude of current up to 2 A, and with small jitter. The cathode and driving electrodes (grids) are taken from generator triode or tetrode. The possibility of generating electron pulses with a current of up to 2 A and duration of 0.6–0.7 ns (on the level of half height) is demonstrated in this work. For this aim we have applied the method of adding harmonic signal of fundamental frequency (360 MHz) which one is equal to double frequency of bunching and accelerating resonators (180 MHz) and signal of fourth subharmonic (90 MHz) of fundamental frequency. This method excludes jitter, which exists in the traditional switch circuits, and gives the possibility to control the amplitude of electron current.

articleTitle: Fabrication of porous ceramic membrane by using pulsed wire discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Gas selective filter has been successfully developed by depositing ultrafine nanosize powders on a porous substrate heated. The powders were produced by pulsed wire discharge, and floated in the gas. Evacuation through the substrate resulted in the accumulation of the powder on the substrate. The powders were sintered on the heated substrate on which the porous membrane was formed. Gas separation experiments showed that gas permeation ratios have been found to be the square root of the ratio of the molecular masses of respective gases. Furthermore, Knudsen flow took place in the filter, which enables us to separate gases of different molecular mass.

articleTitle: Investigation of perspectives of megaampere currents breaking of lowinductive storage using plasma current opening switches at explosive experiments on “POTOK” facility
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: MCG peculiarity, as a source of initial current is determined by low inductance of 20–40 nH (voltage of ∼100 kV) in accumulation contour. To simulate current breaking process in this conditions, and to obtain necessary voltages of ∼2MV for creation of complex EMIR forming system, it is necessary to realize high voltage amplifications in ∼20 times, and energy in ∼10 times. Calculated optimization of the scheme of explosive experiment on MCG current breaking of ∼2MA amplitude and ∼1 µs duration using POS is performed. Results of laboratory development of explosive experiment scheme, are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Nonlinear theory of the resistive high-current plasma-filled diode
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Exact solutions to the set of nonlinear two-fluid MHD equations describing the physical problem of a steady current flow in a two-dimensional resistive plasma-filled diode are obtained and investigated. Even though, in the course of investigation, the class of solutions becomes narrower, the final solution is derived as an exact solution to the initial set of equations. Such factors as the representation of the conductivity in a fairly general form, the allowance for current interactions, and a sufficiently wide scope of effects describable analytically make it feasible to reveal possible important situations to which the approach developed might be implemented practically.

articleTitle: Characteristics of CrN films prepared by pulsed laser deposition
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Chromium nitride (CrN) films have been successfully prepared by pulsed laser deposition (PLD). Experiment was carried out by changing the substrate temperature from R.T. to 600°C. The hardness of the films increased gradually with an increase in the substrate temperature up to 400°C, above which it decreased rapidly. Furthermore, the maximum value was HV∼2000. The rapid decrease in the hardness induced at the formation of ellipsoidal grains. The boundaries of these grains seem to be structural defect.

articleTitle: Longitudinal ion source with beam autocompensation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The longitudinal Hall-type ion source with cold electrodes are described. The source generates compensated hollow oval ion beam of 600 mm length and 50 mm width with the energy within the range of 1– 2 keV and current density of 5–20 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The electrons compensating ion beam are generated in additional gas discharge that is excited in the region of transverse magnetic field localization near the cathode surface. It allows one to decrease the potential of dielectric surface from 700–800 V to 100–150 V, when the ion beam energy is 1 keV. The device is successfully used for low-temperature ion beam treatment of dielectric materials and plastic rolls without damages caused positive surface charges.

articleTitle: Virtual Cathode Oscillator under various cathode radii with intense relativistic electron beam
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It has been reported that the virtual cathode is formed when the electron beam current in the drift region exceeds the space charge limiting current. In this study, the axially-extracted virtual cathode oscillator, which is new conceptual device and the ultra-high power microwave generator consists of the “Chundoong” intense relativistic electron beam pulser (Max: 600 kV, 88kA, and 60 ns duration). In this experiments, Maximum power of extracted microwave is about 520 MW and its conversion efficiency about 8.2 % under cathode radius of 2.5 cm and the Anode-Cathode (A-K) gap is 5 mm. It has been also found that the propagating microwave mode is the combination of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> and the other higher mode based on the electric field(E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>) profile versus cathode radius. The dominant microwave frequency is shown to be 6.07 GHz from this experiment.

articleTitle: Generation on broadband radio pulses by a new type reflex triode with a virtual cathode
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results are presented of the development and experimental study of a new type reflex triode with a virtual cathode. In this device, a discharge excited along a ferroelectric surface is used as a source of electrons and loop antennas are used for emitting radiation. Generation of broadband radio pulses with a central frequency of ∼300 MHz and power of ∼80 W is achieved.

articleTitle: Observation of double pulse discharge for excimer laser excitation with gas flow
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The double pulse discharge has been demonstrated in a gas flow with velocity of 200 m/s which is generated by Ludwieg tube. A gas mixture of helium and argon is used to simulate the excitation discharge of excimer lasers. The shock waves and the gas density perturbation between the two successive discharges have also been visualized by using the shadowgraph technique with the high-speed image-converter camera. The second discharge at an equivalent pulse repetition frequency (f ) of 10 kHz becomes an arc through the heated column which is generated by the first discharge. At f = 5 kHz, the glow discharge can be produced between the electrodes, however, an arc is also observed through the heated column which locates somewhat downstream of the electrodes. Only glow discharge is succeeded at f = 3 kHz. These results clearly demonstrate that the heated column has decisive effects on the stability of repetitive pulse discharge.

articleTitle: Dynamical behavior of higher harmonic generation from a picosecond laser produced solid surface plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have investigated the efficiency of the fifth order harmonics from solid surface plasma by varying the electron density gradient using two 2.2 ps, 1054 nm laser pulses. A 5 ps time difference between the prepulse and main pulse results in an increase in the harmonic signal by a factor of 2–3, which then decreases for time delays greater than 10 ps. Experiments and calculations are presented that demonstrate a strong dependence of the conversion efficiency on the plasma scale length.

articleTitle: Synthesis of nanosize powders of aluminum nitride by pulsed wire discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Using a thin wire of aluminum, we have successfully synthesized the aluminum nitride powders in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> mixed gas. The powders were characterized by X-ray diffraction and specific surface area measurement. The results of X-ray diffraction indicated that the synthesized powders consists of würtzite aluminum nitride. In the powders synthesized in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas weak peak intensity of aluminum nitride was observed. However, it is significantly increased using the mixed gas of N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The average particle sizes were 30 ∼ 70 nm.

articleTitle: Fusion with magnetic implosion of thermonuclear targets
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The comparative analysis of positive and negative features of systems with the magnetic compression of the thermonuclear fusion target (MAGO/MTF) aimed at solution of the controlled thermonuclear fusion (CTF) problem is presented. The niche of the MAGO/MTF system among the other CTF systems in the parameter space of the energy delivered to the target and the time of its input into the target is shown. This approach was investigated at RFNC-VNIIEF for more than 15 years by means of the unique technique applying explosive magnetic generators (EMG) as the energy source to preheat fusion plasma and accelerate a liner for compression of the preheated fusion plasma to the parameters required for ignition. EMG based sys tems produce the fusion neutrons already and their relatively low cost and record energy yield enable the full scale experiments to study possibility of ignition threshold achievement without construction of expensive stationary installations. Short review of the milestone results on the way of CTF problem solution in the MAGO/MTF system is made.

articleTitle: Development of numerical code for plasma simulation within the frame of electron magnetohydrodynamics
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The 2D plasma simulation results within the frame of EMHD theory are presented. The numerical system includes electron hydrodynamics, Maxwell equations, and a set of equations for electron temperature evolution. The code is planned to be used for simulations of EMHD effects in Plasma Opening Switch (POS) and Z-pinch plasmas, as well as for modeling of the magnetic field generation in laser-produced plasmas.

articleTitle: Development of a double pulse generator using an air core transformer with a magnetic switch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new type of double-pulse generator is proposed for the generation of high power pulses with extremely short inter-pulse repetition interval. In this system, an air-core step-up transformer is used with a magnetic switch and a pulse-forming line, which is charged in the double-resonance mode. A small system was constructed to demonstrate the production of double pulses experimentally. The system contains two first stage capacitors of 150 nF each, a 1∶15 air-core step-up transformer, a magnetic switch using cobalt based amorphous core, a second stage capacitor of 1.6 nF, and an 80 Ω load. Double-pulses 100 ns wide, peak voltages of 85 kV (first pulse) and 90 kV (second pulse) have been successfully generated with an interval of 3.75 µs between pulses, when the first stage capacitors were charged to 14 kV (for first pulse) and 17 kV (for second pulse).

articleTitle: Nonthermal plasma chemical processing assisted by catalysis and adsorption
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Nonthermal plasma reactions assisted by catalysis or adsorption were investigated by using a reactor packed with ceramic pellets, mainly BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, mixed with catalyst or adsorbent pellets. The reaction conducted was the decomposition of benzene in air at atmospheric pressure and at room temperature. Using the pellets without a catalyst or adsorbent, the decomposition activity was increased with an increase in the dielectric constant of the pellets and the byproducts of CO and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O were revealed to be produced from lattice oxygen of the pellets. In catalyst-hybrid reactors packed with a mixture of BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> or metal catalyst on Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, the decomposition gave the reduction of byproducts such as CO and N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O. In adsorbent-hybrid reactors packed with a mixture of BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and Molecular Sieves, the formation of NOx was reduced. Based on the formation of the main product of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, a remarkable increase of the decomposition activity was found in the adsorbent-hybrid reactors while a slight increase in the catalyst-hybrid reactors. The decomposition energy efficiency in the adsorbent-hybrid reactor could be improved if the adsorption and plasma discharge were carried out cyclically at optimized intervals.

articleTitle: A continuous pulsed neutron source from dpf device
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A 2.2 kJ repetitive plasma focus device (DPF-2.2) as a continuous pulsed neutron source is presented. Time integrated and time resolved neutron diagnostic techniques were used to investigate the characteristics of the neutron emission at repetitive-rate as one shot per minute. The average neutron yield per shot of (5.14±3.02)×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> and the maximum yield of 2.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> were obtained at the optimum deuterium filling pressure. In comparison with the neutron yield in single mode, the average neutron yield operated continuously for 50 shots without purging the gas is almost the same. The time resolved measurement of the neutron pulse indicated that both the hard X-ray and neutrons are emitted from plasma focus at the same instant and the width of neutron pulse (FWHM) changes slightly from 50 to 53 ns.

articleTitle: Development of a low-energy large-aperture electron beam generator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This research has been carried out to develop a low-energy large-aperture pulsed electron beam (LELAEB) generator, for industrial applications, for example, waste water cleaning, flue gas cleaning, pasteurization, etc. One of the most important features of this electron beam generator is the large electronbeam cross section, up to 200 cm2. In this research, a LELAEB generator of 200 keV was designed and setup, and a large-aperture electron beam was obtained in air outside of the generator. The electron beam current of this LELAEB generator was measured at the several different conditions.

articleTitle: Foil acceleration by intense, pulsed, ion-beam ablation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High pressure, high temperature ablation plasma produced by intense, pulsed, ion-beam has been used to accelerate thin foil target. Pulsed ion beam with energy density in the range of 100 ∼ 4000 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was irradiated on aluminum target with thick of 50 ∼ 100µm. The time-of-flight technique was used to measure the velocity of the accelerated target foil. The maximum target velocity of ∼ 7.7 km/s was obtained. The ablation pressure obtained from the target speed was ∼13 GPa. The target velocity was found to be almost proportional to beam energy density. As an application of the high pressure generated by ablation plasma, the crystalline structure characteristics of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) was studied under the irradiation of pulsed ion beam.

articleTitle: Leaked electrons from virtual cathode oscillation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Investigated are the properties of leaked electrons from virtual cathode oscillation. It is found from the simulation that most leaking occurs from the radial edge of the beam, so that the leaked beam forms an annular beam. An axial bunching was also observed. The average leaked current was close to the space charge limiting current, and the energies of the electrons at the end of the drift tube were a fraction of the injected energies, and were nearly independent of the injection currents. A preliminary experimental result seems to support these simulation results

articleTitle: Influences of floating particles on high-pressure, pulsed glow discharge for excimer laser excitation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The floating particles produced by the high-pressure, pulsed glow discharge on KrF excimer laser excitation have been visualized by the pulsed-laser scatter method. The double-pulse discharge experiments have also been carried out to study the effects of the floating particles on the discharge instabilities. The particles with diameter of the order of 100 µm are observed in the discharge region just after the discharge. The number density of the particles increases to ∼ 3 particle/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 200 ms after the discharge, and then decreases to ∼ 1 particle/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 500 ms. In the double-pulse experiment, the probability of arc in the second discharge reduces from 300 ms after the first discharge. It has been clearly demonstrated that the floating particles of the order of 100µm hardly affect the discharge characteristics.

articleTitle: Induction module with voltage modulation and repetition capability for ion acceleration
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: At low energy region of high current ion accelerators, ion beams must be low current and longitudinally compressed with time to avoid space charge explosion. This means that we have to make a carefully programmed voltage waveform. We propose a voltage synthesis scheme for induction modules to make the waveform shaping and repetitive operation. In this scheme, the voltage is stacked and synthesized by independently driven modules. Each module is composed of a simple L-C based circuit and driven by FETs. The L-C based circuits make sinusoidal waveforms, which enable highly repetitive and low core-loss operation of the induction units. Moreover, this scheme is robust against time jitter of the module switching and non-linear characteristics of the ferromagnetic core materials.

articleTitle: Rep-rated e-beam-pumped KrF laser technology for inertial fusion energy drivers
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Development of a high-repetition-rate (rep-rate) electron-beam (ebeam) pumped KrF laser is described. It aims at pulsed laser outputs of 20 J/80 ns at a rep rate of 1 Hz. Technical efforts are concentrated on diode-foil cooling, which is the key issue of the rep-rate e-beam amplifier technology. E-beam generation experiments have been started with the initial test results of several tens of consecutive shots at 1 Hz. Improvement in the energy-transfer efficiency in the rep-rate pulsed-power systems is also discussed.

articleTitle: Increase of Plasma Opening Switch conduction phase duration
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A creation of the Plasma Opening Switch with a conduction time up to tens of microseconds has a significant importance for the BAIKAL research program which plans using a high current generator with long duration prepulse. To increase the conduction phase various scenarios of POS gap filling with plasma are planned. This includes in series connection of plasma guns. The results of experiments aimed to increasing the charge coming through the POS during the conduction phase are reported at 200 kV Marx generator voltage, 120 kA drive current. And 1 µs current rise time. The prepulse was created by a specially designed pulse forming system.

articleTitle: Optimization of synchronization of MOPA KrF laser system
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper deals with the synchronization of MOPA KrF laser system. In this study, the delay and jitter of all parts of MOPA system has been carried out. Specially, delay and jitter of the switches has been tested under various under-voltage and laser energy, the optimization of the switches operating range is obtained. The results were shown that the jitter of switches is less than 3ns and total jitter of the MOPA system is less than 10ns, therefore synchronization of the MOPA system came true.

articleTitle: Sterilization of materials in the atmospheric pressure pulse corona discharge plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper presents the experimental results on the influence of the pulse corona discharge plasma in the atmospheric pressure air on the cellular culture of Eschericia coli and Bacillus subtilus spores. To excite the pulse corona discharge, a high-voltage nanosecond generator was used. The voltage pulse amplitude was 50 kV, the pulse duration and the pulse repetition rate were 4 ns and 100 Hz, respectively. Polypropylene tips having a form of hollow truncated cones were subjected to sterilization. The culture of cells or spores (∼10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> in number) was put on the internal surface of the cones. The reduction of the number of survivor cells of Eschericia coli by 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> times was reached during 5 – 10 minutes. The total sterilization of the 80 - mm long cones infected by the Bacillus subtilus spores were reached during 30–40 minutes.

articleTitle: Electron beam generation on the MIG water-line facility
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experiments with electron beams have been performed on the MIG water-line pulse generator. Both pinched electron beams and double annular beams without pinching were realized with high reproducibility. The parameters of the beams and bremsstrahlung radiation produced have been measured.

articleTitle: Static and dynamic high-voltage pulse transformers
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The Marx generator is commonly used when it is required to produce high-voltage pulses on a high impedance load. There are however applications in which this will be either too costly or not useful for remote applications and the present paper describes two novel techniques to overcoming these difficulties. Theoretical and experimental results show that high-voltage pulses with rise times of a few tens of nanoseconds can be generated using these techniques.

articleTitle: Pulsed power technology and its applications at EDI, Nagaoka
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Recent activities of pulsed power technology and its applications are overviewed. Using high density ablation plasma inherent to short range of ion beam in targets, we have successfully prepared crystallized thin film of B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>C by ion beam evaporation, which is characterized by hardness, wear resistant, and stability at high temperature. Fullerenes have been prepared as well. Ultrafine nanosize powders have been synthesized by pulsed wire discharge. Flue gas treatment of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> has been succeeded by intense pulsed relativistic electron beam. Foil acceleration has been observed to be ∼ 8 km/s with the ablation pressure of 13 GPa. Pulsed laser deposition was used to prepare (Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1∼x</inf>,Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>)N films. The AlN solubility limit was found to be 77 at.% AlN. The hardness of the films increases with x up to 0.75, and decreases rapidly due to the presence of amorphous structure. Highly repetitive, new pulsed power generator has been operational, with the specifications of 400 kV, 13 kA, 120 ns, 1 pps.

articleTitle: Review of intense light-ion beam production, transport and focussing
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper we describe the status of intense light ion beam production, transport and focussing. We summarise the progress achieved in our understanding of two-stage ion acceleration. A rather consistent view of the injector gap physics has appeared through improved numerical and analytical modelling combined with detailed temporally and spatially resolved field and particle density measurements in the acceleration gap. This needs to be extended to the post-accelerating gap by conducting more systematic experiments at high power and high voltage. Especially a complete understanding of constraints due to limiting voltages and the coupling of instabilities from the injector- to the post-accelerator-gap must still be obtained. We also discuss the efforts to produce clean and large area sources for ions with masses greater than one. It is proposed to tolerate a certain degree of source contaminants, but burying them temporarily under an injected gas or vapour layer. Experimental evidence for self-pinched transport has been demonstrated for the first time at NRL. However more detailed measurements of the dynamics and magnitude of net current formation and transport efficiency seem necessary.

publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams

publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams

articleTitle: Preface
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams (BEAMS 2000) took place in Nagaoka, Japan, on June 25 – 30, 2000. The conference session was held at Hotel New Otani Nagaoka. As is similar to the previous BEAMS conferences, the conference proceeded in a single session, and the papers were given by oral (invited and contributed) and poster presentations. The conference covered the topics on the physics and technology associated with intense pulsed charged particle beams, which involved pulsed power and accelerator technology, pulsed ion and electron beams, diodes, inertial confinement fusion, electron beams, pulsed radiation sources, liner implosions, free electron lasers, high-power microwave, beam-target interaction, diagnostics, models and simulations, X-ray sources, z-pinches, and various industrial applications. The most noticeable movement at BEAMS 2000 was that the number of the papers in the industrial applications increases significantly. Particularly, novel applications were proposed and discussed using pulsed power and particle beams, such as in materials science, chemical, medical, and biological science, civil and environmental engineering, and so on. Totally, 261 papers were presented (58 oral and 203 posters) by 262 participants from 13 countries. Most of these papers are included in these proceedings and some of them are published in the Japanese Journal of Applied Physics, Vol. 40, No. 2B (Special Issue on Pulsed Power and Beam Technology, February, 2001).

articleTitle: Z-pinch optical guiding for GeV electron acceleration by laser wakefield
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Propagating laser pulses over distances larger than vacuum diffraction length is a critical issue for laser wakefield acceleration (LWFA). A new method of optical guiding using fast Z-pinch have been proposed for the GeV LWFA experiment. The feasibility of the guiding of high intensity laser pulses using this method has been experimentally demonstrated over a distance of 2 cm corresponding to 12.5 times the Rayleigh length.

articleTitle: Characteristics of soft X-rays generated with small gas puff Z-pinch device
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The soft X-rays ranged from 2.33 to 4.37 nm are interested in an application for the X-ray microscopy. In order to investigate the soft X-rays ranged in these wavelengths, we newly constructed a small gas-puff Z-pinch device, and investigated the characteristics of it. The experiments were performed with silicon nitride membranes, which were passed through the soft X-rays ranged in these wavelengths.

articleTitle: Roles of nonstationary electrophysical processes in e-beam driven VUV-lasers on rare gas dimers
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of numerical research, carried out for studying of influence of ionization and excitation of argon atoms by high-current beam electrons and secondary plasma electrons, receiving energy from an internal electrical field, on dynamics of excimers are informed.

articleTitle: Pulsed glow discharge for surface treatment
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The transition of high-current glow to an arc and the energy dissipated on the glow phase caused by static breakdown in uniform-field gaps of up to 2 cm has been investigated in dry-air at gas pressures of 1–20 Torr. A low inductance capacitor of 1.89µF and a discharge apparatus with a co-axial configuration were used to produce a transient glow discharge with a current in excess of 400 A. Results showed that the high-current glow discharge occurred at a cathode current density of 3.2 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is almost two orders larger than the predicted value from Cu-air normal glow data of j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>=240×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> [A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>]. The transition from the glow to an arc starts to develop in the discharge region near the cathode. The energies dissipated in the discharge or in the cathode fall region during the glow phase depend on the gas pressure and/or the gap length. However, the dissipated energy density in the cathode fall region during the glow phase is almost constant with the gas pressure and the gap length, with a value of 0.035 J/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> used in the experiment.

articleTitle: High-current heavy-ion accelerator system and its application to material modification
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A high-current heavy-ion accelerator system has been developed to realize intense particle fluxes for material modification. The facility of a tandem accelerator attained 1 mA-class ion current both for negative low-energy ions and positive high-energy ions. A negative ion source of the key device is of plasma-sputter type, equipped with multi-cusp magnets and Cs supply. The intense negative ions are either directly used for material irradiation at 60 keV or further accelerated up to 6 MeV after charge transformation. Application of negative ions, alleviating surface charging, enables us to conduct low-energy high-current irradiation to insulating substrates. Since positive ions over MeV are irrelevant to the Coulomb repulsion, the facility as a whole meets high-current irradiation into insulators over a wide energy range. Application of high flux ions provides technological merits not only in efficient implantation but also in different material kinetics. Other characteristics of the system are co-irradiation of intense laser and in-situ detection of kinetic processes. For the material modification, we present nanoparticle fabrication in insulators, and synergistic phenomena by co-irradiation of ions and photons.

articleTitle: Development of high current laser ion source for heavy ion fusion
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We examined beam optics and emittance of a KrF laser ion source with a pepper-pot method. From copper plasmas produced by 2–4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup>-W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> laser irradiation, ion beams of ∼10 mA were extracted over 20 µs. Stability of the beam optics strongly depended on the flux balance(perveance matching) in the extraction gap. We achieved stable extraction by choosing adequate voltage and source plasma flux. A simple charge-state analyzer using a micro-channel plate (MCP) showed that the ion beams contained Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> dominantly.

articleTitle: Transportation of a low-energy, high-current electron beam in a long plasma channel
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of investigations on the transportation of low-energy (10–30 keV), high-current (/20 kA) electron beam formed in a gun with an explosive-emission cathode and a plasma anode based on high-current reflected discharge are presented. The possibility of transportation of such a beam in a plasma channel of length more than 0.5 m has first been demonstrated. The total energy of the beam per pulse achieved 300 J, which makes up 25% of energy stored in the high-voltage pulse generator. The influence of the current of the reflected discharge on the beam energy density distribution has been investigated, and it has been shown that the improvement of this distribution can be attained by varying the discharge current.

articleTitle: Intense-heavy-ion-beam transport through an insulator beam collimator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We study an intense-heavy-ion-beam transport through an insulator beam guide by a particle simulation in heavy ion inertial confinement fusion. we have proposed a new system for an electron and proton beam transport using an insulator beam guide. We apply this system to a Cs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> beam transport and a Pb<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> beam transport. An intense heavy ion beam creates a local electric field on the insulator inner surface, and generates a plasma on the surface of the insulator guide. Electrons are extracted from the plasma, and the beam charge is effectively neutralized by the electrons. The electron extraction is self-regulated by the net space charge of the beam. Consequently, an intense heavy ion beam can be efficiently transported by the proposed simple system.

articleTitle: Heaven-light IIA, KrF laser facility
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: HL-IIA KrF laser system is rebuilt, based on the HL-II electron beam accelerator. The pulse power system, including a V/N type laser triggered gas switch and two 10Ω output lines, is described. The system is being testing and adjusted. Under dummy condition, it has reached the design levels.

articleTitle: Low-emittance emission of energetic multiple charged ions from short-pulse-laser produced plasmas
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Emission of multi-MeV multiple-charged ions from a target irradiated by a short laser pulse in the range of intensity 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16−20</sup>W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is investigated via a full kinetic particle-in-cell simulations including transient plasma ionization. The anisotropy of the velocity distribution of hot electrons, which dominate the ion acceleration, is found to enhance the ion energy and improve the emittance. Ions over MeV energy are accelerated from non-low-Z matter with up to a 10% conversion from laser energy. A high current, 1 ps duration, short-laser-pulse driven contact ion source based on the modification of the target surface via the laser-induced spallation is discussed.

articleTitle: Three waves theory in virtual cathode oscillator (VCO)
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The linear and nonlinear dispersion relations for the microwave in VCO have been obtained when the complex motion of electron is simplified to the motion of a single charge sheet with time-dependent charge number. It is found in the linear dispersion relation that the field with only one mode in VCO can't grow. Meanwhile, it is shown that there are two modes at least growing simultaneously in VCO. In the case of only two growing waves, the pumping wave which supplies energy is produced by the oscillation of the charge in virtual cathode (VC). This is similar to the matching condition of three waves interaction. The frequency of the pumping wave is the interval between the two growing waves.

articleTitle: The project of high power submillimetr-wavelength free electron laser
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A 100-MeV 8-turns accelerator-recuperator intended to drive a high-power infrared FEL is under construction in Novosibirsk now. The first stage of the machine includes one-turn accelerator-recuperator that contains full RF-system.

articleTitle: Beam transport experiment in JLA induction linac for a MM-meter wave FEL
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An X-band FEL study with the beam energy of 2.0 MeV are undergoing now.
