In order to get a low beam emittance at the beam current of 1kA, the diode design of 1kA in JAERI Large current Accelerator Induction Linac is carried out by EGUN code. To avoid electric discharge on the upper part of wehnelt electrode, the diode chamber and the wehnelt radius are designed under the radial electric field E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of less than 180 kV/cm. The diode chamber size of a φ508 mm diameter and the wehnelt diameter of φ188 mm are decided. In the optimized diode design, the beam current of 1kA and the normalized emittance of 2.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> π mm-mR are obtained.

articleTitle: Hard alloy treatment affect by ion-focused beam on the process of wear-resistant coating
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In the paper the experimental results on investigation of combined process of hardening of hard alloy cutting tools using a pulsed high-power ion beam are presented. The basis of the process is the pretreatment of a surface of working section of a tool by the beam with the current density up to 300 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the subsequent deposition of wear resistance coverings. This leads to the improvement of operational characteristics of the tools compared with coated tools.

articleTitle: Research on transverse impedances of induction accelerating cavities
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Beam Breakup Instabilities(BBU) resulting from the interaction between electron beams and accelerating cavities will deteriorate beam quality, and transverse impedance reflects the degree of such interaction. This paper describes our research on transverse impedance of three different induction accelerating cavities. First the so-called coaxial bi-wires method was applied to measure the three cavities, then MAFIA code was used to simulate these cavities, finally measured data and simulation results are compared and found fit each other well.

articleTitle: X-ray emission induced by 60 keV high-flux negative copper ion implantation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: X-ray emission induced by high-flux 60 keV negative Cu ion implantation into silica glasses (a-SiO2) has been studied in an energy range of 0.6 – 20 keV. At low ion fluxes, the emission spectrum consists of a strong Cu(L) line at 0.95 keV only, without Cu(K) and Si(K) lines. The result is explained by the electron promotion through the quasi-molecule formation. With increasing the ion flux, new peaks appear at 1.8, 2.5 and 3.2 keV. These peaks are ascribed to the sum-peak effect under high-flux implantation. Judging from the cross-sections and the time dependence, the observed Cu(L) X-ray is concluded to be generated via Cu-O collisions.

articleTitle: Microwave ignition of wet explosives for hypervelocity
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper proposes a new gas accelerator which accelerates a projectile to high velocity along a tough wave guide by dielectrically ignited explosion wave. Though any explosives would be a potential candidate for generating pressure wave along the wave guide, a charge whose reaction products is as light as possible should be desirable from the view point of attaining high velocity. An example of such explosives is produced by mixing properly with water, ammonium nitrate and alcohol. This charge will be called WANA in short in this paper.

articleTitle: Measurement of local electric fields in high power ion diodes with resonantly excited probe beam atoms
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An atomic probe beam diagnostic for local electric field measurements across the accelerating gap of the KALIF applied-B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> high power proton diode is under development. It is based on the injection of a collimated pencil-like beam of Li-atoms produced by laser-evaporation from a LiF-target. To achieve the desired sensitivity down to a few hundred kV/cm the atoms are resonantly excited in a two-step process with two broadband dye lasers to the 3d-level. The emitted 3d-2p resonance line splits into five components (of which two coincide) in the diode electric field. The local electric field is inferred from the degree of Stark splitting of these lines. Evaluating the m=0,1 components, fields between 200 kV/cm and 1 MV/ cm can be determined, while the m = 2 component is suitable for fields between 1 and 4 MV / cm. Test measurements at the KALIF-diode have demonstrated that adequate spectral line intensities can be achieved without affecting the diode operation by too much Li-vapour. However, the fluorescence line vanishes as soon as voltage occurs in the diode. Possible causes of this line evanescence are discussed.

articleTitle: Improvement of current efficiency of ion sources based on Penning discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It is shown that the loss of a longitudinal symmetry of magnetic field distribution in respect to the center of the Penning discharge system causes change of electrostatic potential distribution in the discharge gap leads to appearance of asymmetry of current magnitude to the cathodes of the Penning cell, change of magnitude of current density and energy distribution of the ion beam extracted in a longitudinal direction. The use of an inhomogeneous magnetic field which is longitudinally asymmetrical concerning electrodes of the system allows to increase current efficiency of Penning ion sources from 0,2 to 0,55.

Author Keywords: current efficiency of Penning ion beam source

articleTitle: Multimode interaction in Cerenkov generators with overmoded one-sectional slow-wave structures
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Interaction of electron beam with electromagnetic field of four longitudinal modes near the π-type oscillations of a TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-mode has been investigated by means of a nonlinear time-domain hybrid code in the overmoded one-sectional slow-wave structures. The results of numerical simulation are compared with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Accelerator complex with 200 MeV-synchrotron and 10 MeV tandem at the Wakasa-wan energy research center (WERC)
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Accelerator complex of the WERC is now operational. Researches such as the radiation therapy, material science and radiation biology are covered initially.

articleTitle: Research on the correlation between surface morphology and bombardment energy of ar ion to substrates in Fe films prepared by ion beam sputtering
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The surface morphology of the Fe films have been investigated in detail by controlling the condition of a dual ion beam sputtering. The voltage for Ar bombardment V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> was varied in the range of 80–2000 V. The surface morphology and the roughness of the film apparently depended on V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>. The roughness parameter Ra on the film surface was sensitive on V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf>, and was in the range between 0.5 and 15 nm. The temperature near the bombarded position on the film surface, which was calculated by heat equation reached the melting point of Fe at V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</inf> in the range from l00 to 200 V. This model of the thermal spike may estimate the optimum condition of ion bombardment for Fe film deposition.

articleTitle: Fast power semiconductor devices for pulsed power applications
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Semiconductor power devices with fast turn-on characteristics are appearing in the market. The issues in developing the devices for pulsed power applications such as gate driving technique and characterization of the devices, are summarized. SI-thyristors were characterized as a fast high current switching device. A stacked SI-thyristor switching unit was designed and tested that was operated with a repetition rate of 2kHz. Temporal and spatial behavior of carrier number densities in a silicon wafer was measured by the free-carrier absorption method with a pulsed YAG laser.

articleTitle: Design of a modular experiment based on LTD concept for flux compression evaluation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The CEG is evaluating the potential of the flux compression concept in the µs range for high power X-ray generators. A proof-of-principle small experiment, named ECF1 was built (2,5 MA in an inductive load). Special tools were developed allowing manufacturing of specific liner (up to 15 cm long, 10 cm diameter, 432 wires as small as 10,4 µm Al). The CEG is designing now a more powerful experiment based on the same principle, with a new version of LTD stages developed at CEG, and a new experimental chamber allowing the test of different configuration of flux compression.

articleTitle: Investigation of plasma fluxes parameters, realized at current pulses breaking by plasma current opening switch on “KOVCHEG” complex facilities
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of experimental and calculating-theoretical investigations of plasma fluxes parameters, generated during plasma current opening switches (POS) operating on KOVCHEG facility, are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Optical observation of gas discharge induced by high-power and short-pulsed microwave
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The temporal and spatial evolution of gas discharge induced by a high-power, short-pulsed microwave (HPM) was observed by a high-speed image converter camera. The HPM with the peak power of 20MW, frequency of 13GHz, and pulse duration of 14ns was irradiated uniformly into a gap between two spherical electrodes biased to a DC voltage less than a gap breakdown voltage. The streak pictures show two different breakdown mechanisms depending on air pressure. In the high-pressure region over about 300 Torr, the microwave-induced discharge begins at the several spots on the gap axis. When these local discharges grow to link together each other, the gap breakdown occurs. The gap breakdown is delayed about 30 – 300 ns depending on gas pressures and applied DC voltages. In the low-pressure region less than 300 Torr, on the other hand, two-stage breakdown occurs. In the first-stage, a single large discharge luminescence appears in the gap center at the same time as the microwave injection and is followed by another discharge between the first discharge and both electrodes. After a few microseconds of the first-stage discharge, the second-stage discharge following the gap breakdown appears.

articleTitle: Flue gas treatment by pulsed relativistic electron beam
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The environmental problem in the earth such as acid rain is one of the important problem to be solved. Large amount of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> is produced by electric power plants, ironworks and diesel engines, which is the serious problem of the environment. The removal of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> has been studied by using intense pulsed relativistic electron beam (IREB). With the initial NO concentration of 100 ppm and pressure of 120 kPa, ∼ 50 % of NO is removed by 10 shots of IREB. The NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">X</inf> removal efficiency does not depend on the initial NO concentration and the electron energy.

articleTitle: Behavior of the gas-puff z-pinch plasma during the initial phase of discharge in IPP method
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Previous gas-puff z-pinch experiments in our study showed that spatial stability of hot spots in radial direction was obtained by using an inductive pulsed power generator. However, it was confirmed that the injected gas was expanded to radial direction during initial phase of discharge. Therefore it was thought that the compressing process and z-pinch characteristics were influenced by the shape of the injected gas column. In this study, pinching phenomenon during initial phase of discharge was observed by changing the gap length and delay time which was defined as a time from gas injection to discharge onset. Framing photographs of initial compressing phase of the z-pinch plasma revealed that the profile of the initial gas column was influenced by the gap length and delay time. Compression velocity of the initial gas column became slower as the gap length and delay time increased.

articleTitle: The kinetic electron emission induced by fast ions
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It is shown that the distribution function of secondary electrons of ion-induced emission from frond and back surfaces of thin Ag, Cu, Ni foils can be approximated by the power-law function with different power indices in the corresponding energy ranges. The increases of ion energy losses caused the power index to growth in the first energy interval, while in the second energy interval the power index showed the trend to decrease.

articleTitle: Characteristics investigation and optimization of reflecting triode with TEM-type feedback coupling
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The work is devoted to investigation and optimization of characteristics of principally new design of microwave generator diode unit of reflecting triode type with virtual cathode (VC). The main idea is realization of positive feedback coupling using TEM-wave between “generator” part of the reflecting triode (VC formation area) and the area of electron flux formation (cathode - mesh-anode gap).

articleTitle: Characteristics of high-pressure, pulsed glow discharge in gas density depletion
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High-pressure, pulsed glow discharge has been studied for the excitation discharge in TEA gas lasers. The influences of the gas density depletion on the high-pressure, pulsed glow discharge have been investigated eliminating the other instabilities, such as shock waves, residual ions, discharge products and electrode heating. The gas density depletion is produced by utilizing a subsonic gas flow between the curved electrodes. A gas mixture of helium and argon is used to simulate the excimer lasers. The comparison has been made on the single-pulse discharge occurred in the presence of the gas density depletion with the second discharge on the double-pulse experiments in a stable gas. We have found that the big gas density depletion tends to induce the arc without other instabilities. In a stable gas, on the other hand, the second discharge of the double-pulse experiments becomes the arc in much smaller gas density depletion. The arc in the highly repetitive operation might be driven by some factors other than the gas density depletion.

articleTitle: Fabrication of bulk ceramics by high power millimeter-wave radiation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High power 28GHz millimeter-wave radiation was applied to the fabrication of bulk AlN, Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The millimeter-wave radiation enables to sinter these ceramics rapidly at several 100°C lower temperature than the conventional method. The rapid sintering is attributed to the enhancement of atomic migration due to the “non-thermal effect” of millimeter-wave. It is indicated that the millimeter-wave radiation can be available for the efficient process of fabricating bulk ceramics.

articleTitle: Resistive-hall dynamics of microsecond plasma opening switch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Kurchatov Institute has recently developed novel high impedance plasma opening switches. They are capable of producing high voltage multiplication coefficient and can operate in repetitive mode. The paper studies a conduction phase physics for a high-impedance POS. Results of non-linear magnetic field and current penetration are reported. Ohmic and inductive resistance dynamics and corresponding energy losses were determined to improve a contemporary viewpoint on Hall scenario in the pulsed plasma with current.

articleTitle: High-current ion beam induction linac for inertial confinement fusion
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: At present, several methods of obtaining high-current ion beam, which are based on the use of induction accelerators and are applied to inertial controlled fusion (ICF) research, are being considered [1–3]. To date, kiloampere ion beams with energies of several hundred keV have been produced in high-current linear induction accelerators (linac) with collective focusing [4–6]. The power of HHCIBs for ICF purposes must be several orders greater, with rather stringent requirements on beam brightness. Therefore, when developing a driver for ICF on the basis of a high-current linac, it is necessary to investigate a number of important physical problems: (1) the formation of high-current beams in injector; (2) the provision of efficient magnetic insulation for accelerating gaps; (3) charge compensation of the ion beam in the transport channel and in the magneto-insulated accelerating gaps; (4) effective acceleration and stability of the ion beam in accelerating channel; and (5) transport, focusing, and space-time compression of HHCIBs.

articleTitle: Limitations of efficiency of plasma opening switch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper considers principal limitations of plasma opening switch voltage. The decrease of voltage multiplication with energy storage voltage growth has been recently proven. POS voltage is determined by energy spent to remove ions from plasma. Technical opportunities to increase POS voltage use applied magnetic field in the interelectrode gap and charge density decrease. The assessments demonstrate opportunity to use POS as a power intensifying element in the BAIKAL superpower generator creation program.

articleTitle: Laser triggered V/N GAS switch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper is a research on new laser triggered multi-stage switch developed by China Institute of Atomic Energy. This switch specially uses V/N gaps instead of triggered gaps of common switches, which have formed multi channels to reduce the inductance. Electric field simulation calculation is used for optimized designing to make the distribution of electric field reasonable. The result of the experiment shows that the delayed time of laser triggered switch is about 40ns, the time jitter is less than 3ns, over 4 channels can be formed at every stage, the rise time of output pulse is less 15ns.

articleTitle: Plasma destruction of fluorocarbons
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The destruction of fluorocarbons such as chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) is desirable technology because of stratospheric ozone depletion and global climatic changes,. In the present paper, the technologies for CFC destruction in Japan, which are currently in practice, were briefly described. Responding to the global environmental problems, we successfully developed a destruction system using an inductively-coupled radio-frequency plasma. The design of the plasma torch, the performance of the system, and the environmental emissions are also described.

articleTitle: Uniform-fill nozzles for long-implosion-time prs experiments
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have developed uniform-fill nozzles for long-implosion PRS experiments to produce argon K-shell x-rays (photon energy > 3.1 keV). With a 7 cm diameter nozzle, which is appropriate for a 200 ns driver, we have achieved a stable implosion at 180 ns and 4 MA with peak argon K-shell yields exceeding 15 kJ. As previously seen with short (∼100 ns) implosion times, the K-shell yield scales as the fourth power of peak current, I<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. Limited testing with a 10 cm nozzle, which is appropriate for a >250 ns driver, has also achieved a stable implosion.

articleTitle: Generation of an intense electron beam with a sub-nanosecond duration using multi-stage autoacceleration
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An intense relativistic electron beam with a duration of 0.8 ns was obtained by four-stage multi-cavity autoacceleration. The electron beam with an energy of 500 keV and a duration of 12 ns was injected into the coaxial cavities connected tandem with decreasing lengths. And electrons in the last one 16th of its duration was accelerated. The energy of the most accelerated part was 1.1 MeV when a single cavity was used at each stage. The energy increased to 1.3 MeV when the same length cavities were added to each stage.

articleTitle: Repetitive pulsed-power generator “ETIGO-IV”
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new repetitive pulsed-power generator “ETIGO-IV” has been developed for the applications in materials science, pulsed ion-beam acceleration, and high-power microwave generation. It is capable of delivering, to a matched load, an output pulse of 400 kV in peak voltage, 13 kA in peak current, and 120 ns in pulsed length, at the repetition rate of 1 Hz. “ETIGO-IV” consists of a high-voltage supply unit, a pulse-forming unit, and a central control unit. In the high-voltage supply unit, the electrical energy of 1.35 kJ stored in the capacitors is delivered, by thyratron switching, to the pulse-forming unit through high-voltage coaxial cables. In the pulse-forming unit, the pulsed high voltage is multiplied by the pulsed transformers and compressed by the combination of a coaxial pulse-forming line and magnetic switches. “ETIGO-IV” is expected to be used for the generation of repetitive, pulsed ion-beam which has potential applications in material processing, such as pulsed ion-beam ablation and pulsed ion-beam surface treatment.

articleTitle: Microwave radiation from IREB-plasma interaction in a dielectric-lined waveguide immersed in a finite axial magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Linear and nonlinear theory are discussed for waves driven by a linear intense relativistic electron beam in a plasma-filled dielectric-lined cylindrical waveguide immersed in a finite strength axial magnetic field.

articleTitle: Influences of shock waves on high-pressure, pulsed glow discharge for excimer laser excitation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The high-pressure, pulsed glow discharge has been studied for further understanding of the excitation discharge on excimer lasers. The influences of shock waves on the discharge have been investigated eliminating the other factors, which may affect the discharge instabilities, such as gas density depletion, discharge products, residual ions and electrode heating. A shock wave of 1.2 in Mach number is produced by utilizing a shock tube with gas mixture of helium and argon in order to simulate the ArF excimer laser. The schlieren photographs of shock wave and direct images of light emitted from the discharge are recorded simultaneously by a high-speed image-converter camera. It is found that, if the shock wave does not reach to but close to the middle of the discharge region, glow discharge occurs only in front of the shock wave. Even if the shock wave passes through the middle of the discharge region, the glow discharge occurs only in front of the shock wave. However, an arc-like filament through the shock front is also produced. If the shock wave passes through the discharge region, the glow discharge can be produced again, however, a surface discharge is also produced between the main electrode and the pre-ionization pin electrode.

articleTitle: Relativistic electron bunch (REB) excitation of wake fields in a magnetoactive plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have been demonstrated that a multiple excess of the accelerated bunch energy ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf> over the energy of the exciting. REB is possible in a magnetoactive plasma at a certain relationship between the parameters of the “plasma-bunch-magnetic field” system owing to a hybrid volume-surface character of REB-excited wake fields, even without using the REBs contoured in the longitudinal direction

articleTitle: Plasma opening switch with isolation by extrinsic magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper demonstrates recent experiments at RS-20 (1 MV, 350 kA, 2 µs) pulse power generator with the plasma opening switch (POS) operating in the extrinsic magnetic field. The influence of the current density and the transmitted charge on the switching voltage at POS is discussed. POS voltage as a function of the Marx voltage under optimal current density and the transmitted charge is examined and extrapolated for greater values. A scheme of voltage composition is for two POS generators is discussed.

articleTitle: Inductive divider of a voltage on Angara-5-1
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The small-sized reliable inductive divider of a pulse voltage of a nanosecond range of a simple design is described. The divider is used for measurement of a voltage on liner unit on installation of Angara-5-1.

articleTitle: Electrohydraulic hole equipment for oil production intensification and detailed seismic prospection
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In the report the design and operation of the new hole electrohydraulic equipment with diameter of 102 mm and energy capacitance of 5 kJ is described. It was developed in 1995–1997 on the request of A.O. “Татнефteгеофизка” by leading experts from Russian Nuclear Center in high-power pulse systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of wires electrical explosion with microsecond current pulses in longitudinal magnetic field
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Tungsten wire explosion in longitudinal magnetic field is studied. It is shown that superposition of magnetic field leads to decrease of initial disturbances. Qualitative agreement of recorded and calculated electrical and optical patterns of wire burst and expansion is obtained.

articleTitle: «coulomb explosion» of electron vortex as an energetic ion source
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new mechanism of a «Coulomb explosion» is proposed on the basis of a new model of the electron vortices in the plasma with the magnetic field, where ions are accelerated by the electric field arising due to the charge separation at the magnetic Debye radius r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf> ∼ B/4πen<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>. The origin of such explosive dynamics is the formation of «holes» in the electron density at characteristic times of the order of ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pe</inf>−1 (ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pe</inf> is the electronic plasma frequency) as a result of the generation of electronic vorticity by the Weibel instability of electromagnetic wave. Calculations of a laser pulse with intensity J ∼ 6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> W/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> show that the ions expand in the radial direction with velocities up to 3.5 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> cm/s.

articleTitle: Electron beam generation on the MIG wire explosion facility
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The 3 MeV electron beam and 75 kA peak current was registered during recent experiments on the MIG wire explosion facility with high reproducibility. The pulse forming system consists of capacitor banks with 240 kJ stored energy, high-voltage linear pulse transformer, intermediate inductive energy storage, wire exploding open switch and high voltage electron diode. 40 kJ electron beam was focused on Ta or Fe targets by selfmagnetic field. Peak dose of 7*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> RAD/sec for 150 ns FWHM was obtained in the experiments. Dose rate of 1.2*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> RAD/sec was obtained on 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> exposed area.

articleTitle: Pulsed power modulator using high voltage static induction thyristor
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Using a high voltage static induction thyristor (SI-Thy), we made a pulsed power modulator. The pulsed power modulator consists of a Blumlein line and a pulse transformer with amorphous cores. To evaluate the performance of the SI-Thy, the rise time of voltage pulse and the energy transfer efficiency from the pulse forming line to a matched load resistor were measured, changing turn-on gate voltages and charging voltages of the pulse forming line. The rise time of output voltage is decreasing with turn-on gate voltage. When a turn-on gate trigger voltage of 100V was applied, the rise time less than 90ns was attained for the charging voltage of 5000V. The energy transfer efficiency is increasing with turn-on gate trigger voltage and the efficiency higher than 90% was obtained for the charging voltage of 5000V under the condition that the turn-on gate trigger voltage is 100V.

articleTitle: Observation of chaotic self-modulation regimes in powerful backward-wave oscillator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Self-modulating regimes of generation in X-band BWO with several megawatt power level was studied theoretically and experimentally. Periodic sinusoidal modulation of the output signal was observed, which became more complicated as the beam current grew, acquired the character of a series of spikes, and then lost its periodicity. The simplification of generation regimes under the further current increasing can be explained by the space charge influence.

articleTitle: Simulation of high power electron linac
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report the results of some calculations on the beam dynamics in the high power linac and discuss them in this paper. The magnet and RF-field in linac had been calculated by mesh method and then the beam dynamics had been calculated by particle tracking method. It is found that the electron beam can be obtained energy of 10 MeV and average power of 28 KW.

articleTitle: Control of x-ray emission from the shotgun z-pinch plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The axial magnetic field was applied to the Ar gas-puff z-pinch for the control of radial dynamics and x-ray emission from the plasma. The K-shell radiations of Ar ions were suppressed and the L-shell radiations were enhanced by the axial field. The suppression of m=0 mode instability was observed by using a framing camera. The characteristic pinch radius was compared with a simple model based on the magnetic pressure balance.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic study of the fast capillary discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The analysis of the time resolved, the spatially resolved, and the spectrally resolved soft X-ray radiation coming out along the axis of the fast capillary discharge is presented.

articleTitle: Characterisation of electron beams produced by crossed-field secondary emission diodes
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The crossed-Field Secondary Emission (CFSE) diode is a compact, simple and cheap source of tubular electron beams in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>A range of currents. The physical mechanism of current production is a self-sustained secondary electron emission. The electron beams produced are characterised by extremely high temporal stability and narrow (∼1.4mm) radial current density distributions. A uniform azimuthal current density distribution j(φ) can be achieved by careful adjustment of the cathode-anode assembly. In non-axisymmetric diodes, the j(φ) distributions are strongly non-uniform and depend not only on the magnitude but also on the direction of the magnetic field. Results of the present research show that the CFSE electron sources are ideal candidates for incorporation into medium and high power microwave devices.

articleTitle: Properties of basaltic fibres after ion irradiation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The outcomes of researches on ion irradiation of basalt fibres by ions C +, N +, O- and influencing of ionic irradiation on a surface energy of basalt fibre are shown.

articleTitle: All solid state and high repetition rate pulsed power system for pulsed power discharge gas treatment
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An all solid state pulsed power system having output voltage of 50kV, voltage rise time of lower than 50ns, repetition rate up to 1kpps, energy per pulse of up to 0.6J has been developed. Using this pulsed power system, pulsed power discharge plasma reactor system has been developed for an industrial odorous gas treatment. Laboratory scale experiments using simulated odorous gas shows that the system developed has higher deodorization performances than traditional adsorption methods. Furthermore, we have obtained successful results in field-tests using a prototype of industrial scale pulsed power discharge plasma deodorizer having treatable gas volume up to 10m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/min.

Author Keywords: all solid state pulsed power system

articleTitle: Steady state of dense sheet Z-pinch with thermal conduction
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The problem of steady state of the sheet Z-pinch was solved, incorporating the thermal conductivity effects. Particularly, the classes of solutions with small plasma pressure and low temperature on the sheet boundary are investigated. There are 3 types of the temperature profiles. Dependence on the pinch plasma parameters is found.

articleTitle: Laser welding with high power lasers combining system
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have developed the high power laser beam combining system with the 10kW class chemical oxygen-iodine laser (COIL) of wavelength 1.315µm and the 6kW class Nd:YAG laser of wavelength 1.064µm. The characteristic of the beam propagation, the combining beam quality and the optics were evaluated. The combining beam providing power was up to over 16kW. The combining beam was used for laser welding of the thick SUS304 stainless steel (10∼20mm) plates. The effects of various welding parameters which were the laser powers, the shielding gases, the welding speeds, the focus positions, welding postures were investigated. The high quality welding results for the 15mm thick SUS304 plates were obtained.

articleTitle: Nanosecond pulses transformer
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Block-diagram and parameters of nanosecond pulse transformer made on coaxial cables and intended for connection pulse voltage generators with large lines of position and obtaining electromagnet TEM-waves of nanosecond duration and also for supply big coaxial water lines and powerful accelerators are described in the report.

articleTitle: Performance of the Negative ion source for JT-60U
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The 500keV Negative-ion based neutral beam injector for JT-60U started the operation in 1996 and has injected so far a neutral beam power of 5.2MW at 350keV for 0.7sec. However there are some issues to be conquered for increasing furthermore the beam power and beam pulse duration time. One of those is source plasma non-uniformity in the arc chamber. Improving the issue, three countermeasures have been conducted. The first is to change an arc discharge distribution through changing arc current resistors which connects in series to each of eight filament cathode groups. The second is masking both ends of the plasma grid with thin molybdenum plates to block beam extraction at the edges. The third is changing arc discharge mode from space charge limited discharge to emission limited which is relatively independent on the plasma condition in the arc chamber. The first two countermeasures have been determined to be effective against the source plasma non-uniformity, and the third is being examined.

articleTitle: Non-quasineutral model of an equilibrium z - pinch
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A radically new equilibrium of z-pinch is proposed, where at the scale r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ∼ √J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> en<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>c / (J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> — the current flowing inside the radius r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf> — the electron density) the strong charge separation arises, which results in the radial electric field. In this equilibrium, the current is transported near the axis at r≤r<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> by the drifting electrons, and at the z-pinch periphery on the scale c/ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pi</inf> — by the ions with the velocity v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">iz</inf> ∼ c (2ZeJ/m<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>), where J - the total current of the z-pinch. In the nonquasineutral core of the z-pinch the radial «temperature» of the ions prove to be of the order of ZeJ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>/c. The lifetime of the nonquasineutral region of the z-pinch is limited by the Coulomb collisions of the radially oscillating ions with electrons. For lack of the magnetic field «frozen-in» effect in ions at the nonquasineutral core the z-pinch instability of the neck-type is absent.

articleTitle: Energy loss of 6 MeV/u iron ions in partially ionized helium plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Energy loss of heavy ions in partially ionized helium plasma has been measured for <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">56</sup>Fe ions of 6 MeV/u energy as a function of incident charge state. The charge states of iron ions were varied between 21 and 25. Electron density of the plasma formed by Z-pinch discharge ranged from 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> to 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. Enhanced stopping in plasma has been observed compared to cold helium gas. The measured stopping power has been analyzed with an equation for partially ionized plasma.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Ti-Al intermetallic compounds films by intense pulsed ion-beam evaporation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In order to examine the possibility of the synthesis of an intermetallic compound thin film by ion beam evaporation (IBE), the synthesis of a Ti-Al system intermetallic compound thin film was tried. The crystal structure and composition of the film were evaluated. By using combined target of Ti and Al, thin film of single phase was not observed. By using alloy target, the Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al film was formed successfully. The Ti<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Al film has been orientated in the (002) plane. The orientation to the (002) plane was strengthened by heating the substrate.

articleTitle: Observations of dense sheet z-pinches
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It was tried to produce the dense sheet z-pinch plasma in order to avoid strong instabilities in a fiber z-pinch. There are two types of sheet z-pinches depending on the formation mechanism: (a) compressional and (b) stretched types. In this experiment the latter type was examined. The sheet z-pinch plasma was observed in the medium pressure region (7 – 20 torr in Hydrogen gas). The pinch similar to plasma focus was also observed at the upside of the plasma sheet. Although it was weaker than that in the plasma focus, it was seems to be sustained for longer period (about 500 ns)

articleTitle: Nanosize Al2O3 powder production by pulsed wire discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Nanosize Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powder was produced by pulsed wire discharge. The discharge was carried out with the peak current of ∼10kA, the pulse length of ∼20µs, and the pulse energy of ∼80J. Nanosize γ-Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> powders have been synthesized by pulsed discharge of metal wires in oxygen as an ambient gas. The powder size and its distribution were able to control by the oxygen pressure.

articleTitle: Compact gas dischargers for well electric equipment
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The design of compact gas discharger used as a component of well electrohydraulic equipment and results obtained in testing them at the voltages up to 50 kV and energies up 5 kJ are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Characteristics of high-current pulsed discharge
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The time-dependent resistance of high-current pulsed arc discharge was obtained accurately by solving circuit equation using measured values of the current and breakdown voltage. The gap length and gas pressure were changed from 0.1 to 2.0 cm and from 200 to 760 Torr, respectively. The arc resistance takes the minimum value at the maximum arc current, and the minimum value can be expressed by a function of maximum current. The initial stages of the discharge (i.e., from 0.1 to 0.6 micro second after sparkover), the equations by Rompe, Vlastos, and Kushner give the accurate predicted values of arc resistances. At later stages after maximum arc current (i.e., from 0.6 micro second after sparkover), the values obtained from the equations by Kushner and AWA model agree well with the measured value.

articleTitle: Ion currents in ace 4 upstream of POS during opening
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Concern that the plasma remaining upstream of the initial region of plasma injection for the plasma opening switch may adversely impact the performance of the switch has motivated investigation of the properties of this residual plasma. Here a model is introduced and calculations performed to compare with Faraday cup measurements (see Fig. 1) of ion currents in the residual plasma during the high voltage pulse following the end of the conduction phase<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1)</sup>. This model complements the model for ion currents in the conduction phase reported previously reported<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2)</sup>. The calculations are based on the assumption that ions are generated by electron impact ionization of neutrals residing in upstream locations (Fig. 2). The electrons acquire their energy from the switch voltage in the form of an E×B drift in the magnetic field of about seven tesla that exists at the onset of opening.

articleTitle: Correlated stopping of relativistic electron beams in supercompressed DT fuel
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Fundamental features of dynamically 2-correlated relativistic electrons in the MeV energy range and interacting with very dense and hot hydrogenic plasmas of fusion interest are thoroughly investigated. The target is modelled with a Drudelike dielectric function. Longitudinal and undramped pair correlations along overall drift velocity are contrasted to transverse ones decaying exponentially over several tens of target screening length λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf>. Other novel behaviours include a much higher response to target temperature variations, than to density ones, for the ratio of 2-correlated to uncorrelated stopping.

articleTitle: Photocurrent characteristics of oxygenated fullerene thin film
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In order to obtain the higher photocurrent in metal/insulator/semiconductor junction cells, oxygenated fullerene thin films are used as the insulator thin film. The highly oxygenated fullerene thin films are obtained by using RF O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> plasma with cooling system. From the experimental results, it is found that oxygenated fullerene thin films, C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> (x=8, 16, 24, 38, 50 etc.), are obtained by using a laser-desorption time-of-flight mass spectrometer (TOF-MS). By using the 200 nm in thick multilayer fullerene junction film, the photocurrent becomes 30 times larger that of normal fullerene.

articleTitle: NOx removal using ammonia radicals prepared by intermittent dielectric barrier discharge in atmospheric pressure
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The NOx removal was made at a temperature of 950°C by using ammonia radicals. The radicals were efficiently produced by flowing 1–3 % NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> in Ar through the dielectric barrier discharge of a one-cycle sinusoidal (OCS)-wave power source. The discharge was intermittently made between coaxial cylindrical electrodes with a space of 1.5 mm at an applied peak-to-peak voltage of 10–35 kV. At the mixing zone in the reaction chamber the spectrum of the NH radical was observed at 336.7 nm. The radicals were introduced to a reaction chamber, and were mixed with 1000 ppm NOx in N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The NOx reduction increased with increasing the concentration of the NH radical. The dependence of NOx reduction on the duty cycle of OCS voltage was also discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetic field generation in Crab Nebula by PIC simulations
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Intense magnetic field generation in Crab Nebula is studied by 2-D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation. We have proposed mechanism of magnetic field generation by Weibel-type electromagnetic instability. We apply our theory to Crab Nebula and obtain intense magnetic field by 2-D PIC simulation.

articleTitle: Influence of particle fluxes from target on characteristics of intense electron beams
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: When a solid target is irradiated by an intense electron beam, surface processes take place leading to appearance of electron and ion fluxes, which influence on the characteristics of the beam. Electron flux from a target appears as a result of back scattering of beam electrons. Ion flux arises due to ionization of absorbed atoms and plasma formation on the target surface. In this paper results from experimental and numerical investigations of the influence of target particle of fluxes on the characteristics of electron beams from diode configurations are presented. It is shown that reflected electrons decrease the beam current and change also the distribution of the energy deposited by the electron beam into a target. The ion flux changes the spatial and temporal distribution of the beam current density at the target. The initially uniform distribution becomes nonuniform with a sharp maximum at the beam center. The influence of the target particle fluxes have to be taken into account when an electron beam is applied for irradiation of solids.

articleTitle: Preparation of SrAl2O4:Eu phosphor thin films by intense pulsed ion-beam evaporation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: SrAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> activated with Eu phosphors has been known to exhibit highly bright and long-lasting phosphorescence without radioactive materials. In this paper, SrAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Eu thin films have been successfully deposited on Si(100) or graphite substrate by using an intense pulsed ion-beam evaporation technique. The results of X-ray diffraction and photoluminescence suggest that SrAl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:Eu thin films which has a polycrystalline structure can be produced in vacuum, without substrate heating and annealing. The composition and morphology of the films have been analyzed by Rutherford backscattering and scanning electron microscope. From RBS analyze, we have obtained good stoichiometry between the target and the films prepared.

articleTitle: Pulsed electron beams for cleaning air from sulphur-containing impurities
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The advantages of the use of pulsed electron beams for cleaning air from sulphur-containing impurities (CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) are discussed. Experiments with high current nanosecond electron beam and with low current microsecond one were carried out. It was stated that reactions with the involvement of CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are realized by the chain mechanism.

articleTitle: Radioactive reliability of programmable memories
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The aim of this paper is to examine the reliability of EPROM and EEPROM components under the influence of gamma radiation. This problem is significant for military industry and space technology. Total dose results are presented for the JL 27C512D EPROM and 28C64C EEPROM components. There is evidence that EPROM components have better radioactive reliability than EEPROM components. Also, the EPROM's changes are reversible and after erasing process and reprogramming EPROM components are functional. On the other hand EEPROM's changes are irreversible and under the influence of gamma radiation all EEPROM components became permanently nonfunctional. The obtained results are analyzed and explained via the interaction of gamma radiation with oxide layers.

articleTitle: Design of weakly relativistic large-orbit gyrotron with permanent magnet system
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High-harmonic gyro-devices with axis-encircling electron beams known as large orbit gyrotrons (LOG) represent an appealing alternative to the conventional gyrotrons. In this paper, we investigate the feasibility of such device operating with low current and low energy electron beams formed by a novel electron gun with a permanent magnet system. The results from the numerical experiments indicate the possibility to excite TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">41</inf> mode at fourth harmonic of the cyclotron frequency. Simulations predict generation of microwave radiation with frequency 104 GHz and output power near 1 kW.

articleTitle: Bidirectional line pulse generator system for linear induction accelerator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In order to obtain a high-current charged particle beam, a bidirectional line pulse generator system for external pulse injection, which is applicable to a linear induction accelerator (LIA) with line-type cavities, was constructed. The system can attain the energy transfer efficiency of 100% theoretically, because the magnetic cores usually used in conventional LIAs are unnecessary and residual magnetic energy stored in the cavity after completion of the pulse can be made zero. However, the result showed that the waveform obtained experimentally was far from the ideal one and the cause was attributed to an inductance and resistance of a main gap switch, which is a conventional trigatron gas-filled gap switch. Therefore, to obtain an ideal bidirectional voltage waveform, the basic characteristics of a laser-triggered switch using a Q-switched pulsed Nd:YAG laser have been investigated. An experiment with pulse charging of line was carried out in this time taking into account an application to the existing bidirectional pulse generator. The experimental results will be reported.

articleTitle: Design and testing of a 2.4MJ pulse power supply
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this article, the design features and some test results of 2.4MJ pulsed power supply system are described. The power system consists of eight capacitive 300kJ energy modules. Each 300kJ module is composed of six 22kV 50kJ 206uF capacitors. Triggered vacuum switch (RVU-43, VEI) was adopted as a main pulse power-closing switch and its operation characteristics were investigated. As a crowbar circuit, we used three parallel crowbar diode stacks, which are fabricated in coaxial structure with two series 13.5 kV, 60 kA avalanche diodes and two 110mO crowbar resistors. The design features of pulse shaping inductors, charging and dump circuit, and other components will be described. The electrical performances of each component and current output variations into resistive loads will also be presented.

articleTitle: Optical observation of the instability in microsecond gas-puff z-pinch plasmas
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The occurrence of fluid instabilities in gas-puff z-pinch plasmas have been investigated using laser diagnostic systems. An interferometer system was employed to investigate the temporal evolution of the structure in the plasma column during the pinch. The z-pinch plasma was driven by a fast bank, which provided a current of 160 kA at 1.5 µs (T/4). Initially the plasma was formed in a conical shape due to the initial gas distribution. The plasma layer moved toward the z-axis and its shape gradually changed into columnar. The plasma layer splits into two layers on the way to implosion. The inner layer, which was indicated to be shock front, propagated toward the z-axis faster than the outer layer. The outer layer seemed quite smooth while the implosion by the inner layer took place at the z-axis. After the blast from the implosion expanded and came across the outer layer, the disturbance occurred at the outer layer. It is concluded that the plasma instability is significantly influenced by the shockwave rather than the initial gas formation in the case of a microsecond implosion.

articleTitle: Hardening in MgO·3.0Al2O3 by neutron irradiation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: MgO·3.0Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> single crystalline samples were irradiated with fast neutrons in various conditions and the hardness of the irradiated and unirradiated samples was measured with a Vickers hardness tester. The hardness of an as-irradiated sample increased by 23 %. After isochronal annealing, the hardness gradually decreased and mostly recovered to that of the unirradiated one above 600 °C, and fully recovered after annealing at 900 °C. Volume of the sample also increased after the irradiation and changed in the same way as the hardness by annealing. A relation between hardness and density of point defects is proposed and the experimental results agree with the relation. It implies that the point defects pin down dislocations generated by the indentation and increase the hardness of neutron irradiated MgO·3.0Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> samples.

articleTitle: Penetration of a nonlinear electromagnetic wave along the transmission line in a mather-type device
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The dynamics of a plasma with two ion species is analyzed on the basis of hydrodynamics equations in a magnetic field under the condition B<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ≫ 8πp. For this plasma the equations are investigated in the ratio diapason of the plasma density to the magnetic field υ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ii</inf>/ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Bi</inf> < (Z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> M/m)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/4</sup>, when the skin-effect penetration of the magnetic field into the plasma is determined by ion-ion collision. The simultaneous dynamic equations are presented, which describe the diffusive penetration of the magnetic field and the density redistribution of the ion species. The applicability of this equations to the transportation of the current sheath for the ≪plasma focus≫ devices is discussed.

articleTitle: Development of the optimization designed electtron source for 12MV induction linac
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: 12MV Linear induction electron accelerator was built in 1994, its electron beam source is a diode consisting of a velvet cathode and an anode with a tungsten net. A whole series of optimization designs of diode are studied by using the numerical simulation code MAGIC in order to improve the beam quality of electron source and 12MeV LIA, and the optimum diode is concluded by comparing to the results of experiment. In this way, an energy 1MeV, current >3kA, pulse width 100ns (FWHM) intense electron beam can be obtained at the output of the LIA injector.

articleTitle: Beam extraction and characterzation of metal clusters of different charged states
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have succeeded in the generation, extraction and characterization of the cluster beams consisting of the neutral, positive and negative ion niobium clusters over a wide size-range (Nb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>: 1≤n≤1,100). Cluster generation process in different charged states were examined.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of thin foils irradiated by ultrashort pulse laser
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In the development of the x-ray laser, it is expected that uniform high temperature high-density plasmas may be instantaneously generated by using a thin foil target, without the loss of energy by heat conduction inside the target. Here, we present the numerical results of the formation and the expansion of the plasmas due to the irradiation of the ultrashort pulse laser onto a thin foil target.

articleTitle: High-energy electrons generation in laser procuced plasmas
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Emission of high-energy electron beams up to 2 MeV were observed from underdense plasmas produced by focusing high-power short laser pulses (1.8TW, 100fs) on gas jets. The electron beam was collimated in a half angle of 3–4° around the optical axis of the laser beam. The energy of the electrons has the power-law spectrum of E<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3.5</sup>. The production of the high-energy electrons closely correlated with the appearance of the complex filamentary structure of the laser propagation.

articleTitle: NOx removal experiment by pulse electron beam irradiation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> removal in the gas chamber filled with atmospheric pressure NO/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas was investigated by injection of the pulse electron beam of 160keV energy, beam current of 140A, current density of 2A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, pulse width of 0.7 µs and electron beam power of 12.6J/pulse, or the electron beam of 120keV, 10A, 2.5µs and 2.8J/pulse. Optimum energy efficiency of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> removal in NO/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas depends strongly on the operating parameters. The efficiency increased for the large volume of gas chamber, dense initial NO concentration and relatively low electron beam power at small removal ratio. The efficiencies increased to 900nmol/J when the electron beam with 0.1∼0.35J/pulse was injected into the gas mixture of NO(=200ppm)/N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Pulse electron beam source for NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> removal experiment was improved to increase the output electron beam power as compared with the stored energy of the Marx generator. The injected electron beam power increased to 46% of the stored energy by using an active plasma cathode.

articleTitle: Frequency Feature of a Multiwave Cerenkov Generator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper reports the experimental results that conform the previous simulation study on the frequency feature of a Multiwave Cerenkov Generator. The generated microwave is measured within the frequency range of 9.68 ∼ 10.2GHz, with a power level well over 100MW. Also reported is an improved frequency measurement method using two separate signal lines.

articleTitle: Non-axisymmetric radiation from high power backward wave oscillators
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Theoretical and experimental studies of X-band high power backward wave oscillators (BWO's) operating between π and 2π-mode region are presented. The non-axisymmetric HE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode from the BWO operating between π and 2π modes is observed and compared with the numerical results.

articleTitle: Use of the pulsed magnetron sputtering of graphite target for the deposition of DLC films
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The process of ion-assisted deposition of DLC films by pulse magnetron sputtering of a graphite target is described. To realize this method, a pulsed power supply for powering the magnetron discharge and a pulsed high-voltage generator have been developed. High-voltage substrate biasing, synchronized with magnetron current pulses, was used to control the energy of the ions bombarding the substrate surface. Probe measurements of the plasma have shown that the density of the magnetron discharge plasma reaches values of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>. The experiments on DLC films deposition were carried out with using of different kinds of substrates: single-crystal (111) silicon wafers, titanium, stainless steel, glass. The main result of the experiments was the obtaining of a hard, high-adhesive DLC films.

articleTitle: The atlas high-energy density physics project
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Atlas is a pulsed-power facility under development at Los Alamos National Laboratory to drive high-energy density experiments. Atlas will be operational in the summer of 2000 and is optimized for the study of dynamic material properties, hydrodynamics, and dense plasmas under extreme conditions. Atlas is designed to implode heavy-liner loads in a z-pinch configuration. The peak current of 30 MA is delivered in 4 µs. A typical Atlas liner is a 47-gram-aluminum cylinder with ∼ 4-cm radius and 4-cm length. Three to five MJ of kinetic energy will be delivered to the load. Using composite layers and a variety of interior target designs, a wide variety of experiments in ∼ cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> volumes will be performed. Atlas applications, machine design, and the status of the project are reviewed.

articleTitle: Development of high power, frequency tunable, submillimeter wave sources - Gyrotron FU series
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The gyrotrons developed at Fukui University (Gyrotron FU series) are high frequency, high power devices, covering a broad frequency band in the millimeter and submillimeter wavelength region. Currently, the Gyrotron FU series consists of eight gyrotrons. In this paper, we summarize and illustrate some of the achievements of the Gyrotron FU series.

articleTitle: Supra-thermal electron generation by an ultra-intensive laser pulse in inhomogeneous foil plasma
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Relativistic electrons are produced, with energies up to 10 MeV, by the interaction of high-intensity laser pulse with an underdense plasma. With the progress of short-pulse multi-terawatt laser, it has become possible to produce MeV electrons in a plasma. These electrons can be used to apply to medicine and technology. Three-dimensional (3D) particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations were performed to produce supra-thermal electrons.

articleTitle: Electron beam transport system development for multi-terawatt modular x-ray generators
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Electron beam transport is being studied as a means of obtaining high-dose, small-area irradiation from multimodule bremsstrahlung generators. Both grad-B and Z-discharge transport are investigated. Novel methods of obtaining beam compression and beam overlap with grad-B transport have been demonstrated. Efficient Z-discharge transport of high-current beams has been demonstrated for the first time.

articleTitle: Emission properties of metal-ceramic, velvet, and carbon fiber cathodes
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We present results of studies of emission properties of cathodes at accelerating fields of 3 – 6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> V/cm. We investigated cathodes which are made of metal-ceramic, carbon fibers, carbon fabric, velvet or corduroy. Experimental data concerning light emission from the cathode surface, uniformity and divergence of the generated electron beams are presented. Data related to the impedance, power, and energy of diodes operating with these cathodes are given as well. It was found that the tested cathodes, except the cathode made of carbon fibers, showed significant degradation of their emission properties within 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> generator shots. We also present data of the vacuum deterioration as a result of cathode operation.

articleTitle: Revisit to current multiplication due to intense relativistic electron beam-plasma interaction
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Particle-in-cell simulation have been performed to investigate the relation among the beam modulation, the current multiplication, and the two-stream instability in an intense relativistic electron beam (IREB) - plasma system which is in a strong Langmuir turbulence state. The results are used to explain the dependence of high-power broadband millimeter wave radiation emitted from this system on the density ratio of the beam electrons to the plasma electrons.

articleTitle: A new method of ultrashort-wave electromagnetic generation
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper describes a new method of generating a powerful ultrashort-wave electromagnetic radiation; the layouts of electromagnetic generators and the results of their tests are given.

articleTitle: Optical investigation of fast pulsed discharge on surface of ceramics for environmental applications
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Pulsed surface discharge on the surface of ceramics was investigated experimentally. Photon counting method was applied to clarify preceding phase of the discharges. The results indicated the effect of charge injection from electrodes. Pulsed surface discharge reactor for decomposition of nitrogen oxides utilizing honeycomb ceramics was proposed. Framing and streak observation was carried out with image converter cameras. Emission spectra from the discharge were investigated with spectrometer. Uniform surface discharges on honeycomb ceramics were successfully obtained utilizing pulsed power generator with a SI-thyristor.

articleTitle: Flue gas treatment using multipoint barrier discharge with pulse modulator
publicationTitle: 2000 13th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An experimental study on the removal of NOx in flue gas has been carried out using plasma chemical reactions in a dielectric barrier discharge. A multipoint-to-plane geometry is used for electrode to lower the operating voltage. Plasma is produced in a narrow gap by a dielectric barrier discharge at low applied voltage with sinusoidal waveform of 2–3 kV r.m.s.. The configurations of parallel plane electrode and multipoint-to-plane electrode have been compared to provide information an effectiveness of the gas treatment. The experimental result shows that the multipoint-to-plane electrode is more effective than parallel plane at low energy and low operating voltage. The power requirements would be 24 W to remove 200 ppm of NO using multipoint-to-plane geometry, while the power requirement is 177 W by using parallel plane reactor. At the NOx reduction from a 20 kVA diesel engine exhaust gas, the power supply used was mainly composed with rectifier circuits, IGBT and pulse transformers, and 10 kV pulses can be generated at 2.5 kpps (pulses per seconds). The NOx (NO+NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) in the gas exhausted from the diesel engine generator has been reduced up to 10% with electrical efficiency of 28 g/kWh at a flow rate of 1.2 Nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>/min‥
